sentences.zh: 列傳第六十七

translations.literal: Biographies 67
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 67

sentences.zh: 酷吏 ○高閭山 蒲察合住

translations.literal: Cruel Officials: Gao Lushan, Pucha Hezhu
translations.idiomatic: Cruel Officials — Gao Lushan, Pucha Hezhu

sentences.zh: 佞幸 ○蕭肄 張仲軻 李通 馬欽 高懷貞 蕭裕 胥持國

translations.literal: Favorites of Fortune: Xiao Yi, Zhang Zhongke, Li Tong, Ma Qin, Gao Huaizhen, Xiao Yu, Xu Chiguo
translations.idiomatic: Favorites of Fortune — Xiao Yi, Zhang Zhongke, Li Tong, Ma Qin, Gao Huaizhen, Xiao Yu, Xu Chiguo

sentences.zh: 太史公有言：「法家嚴而少恩。

translations.literal: The Grand Historian said: "The Legalists are severe and sparing in kindness."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian once said, "The Legalists are harsh and stinting in mercy."

sentences.zh: 」信哉斯言也。

translations.literal: How true those words are.
translations.idiomatic: How true those words are.

sentences.zh: 金法嚴密，律文雖因前代而增損之，大抵多准重典。

translations.literal: Jin law was rigorous; although the statutes were revised with additions and deletions from earlier dynasties, for the most part they followed severe precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Jin law was severe. Though the statutes were revised from earlier codes, they largely followed the harshest precedents.

sentences.zh: 熙宗迭興大獄，海陵翦滅宗室，鉤棘傅會，告奸上變者賞以不次。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong repeatedly launched great prosecutions; Emperor Hailing exterminated the imperial clan; charges were twisted and forced into alignment; those who reported treachery and submitted denunciations of rebellion were rewarded with extraordinary promotions.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xizong great prosecutions arose again and again; under Emperor Hailing the imperial clan was cut down; charges were twisted to fit; and informers who denounced treason were rewarded with swift promotion.

sentences.zh: 於是中外風俗一變，咸尚威虐以為事功，而讒賊作焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon customs throughout the court and the realm changed entirely; all prized cruelty and severity as achievement, and slanderers and villains arose.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country alike turned to cruelty as a mark of achievement, and slanderers flourished.

sentences.zh: 流毒遠邇，慘矣。

translations.literal: The poison spread far and near — how dreadful.
translations.idiomatic: The harm spread near and far — a dreadful state of affairs.

sentences.zh: 金史多闕逸，據其舊錄得二人焉。

translations.literal: The History of Jin has many gaps and omissions; from the older records only two men can be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Much of the Jin history is lost; from surviving older records only two such men can be named.

sentences.zh: 作《酷吏傳》。

translations.literal: A biography of cruel officials is compiled.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the compilation of the Biographies of Cruel Officials.

sentences.zh: 高閭山

translations.literal: Gao Lushan
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lushan

sentences.zh: 高閭山，澄州析木人。

translations.literal: Gao Lushan was a native of Ximu in Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Lushan was from Ximu in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 選充護衛，調順義軍節度副使，轉唐括、移剌都颭詳穩，改震武軍節度副使、曹王府尉，大名治中。

translations.literal: Selected to serve as a guardsman, he was transferred to be deputy military commissioner of the Shunyi Army; then served as xiangwen for Tangguo and Yila Duzha; was changed to deputy military commissioner of the Zhenwu Army and commandant of the Cao Prince's household, and became administrator of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as an imperial guardsman, became deputy commissioner of the Shunyi Army, then held xiangwen posts under Tangguo and Yila Duzha, and later served as deputy commissioner of the Zhenwu Army, commandant of the Prince of Cao's household, and administrator of Daming.

sentences.zh: 遷汝州刺史，改單州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to prefect of Ruzhou and then transferred to Shanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Ru Prefecture, then transferred to Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 制禁不依法用杖決人者，閭山見之笑曰：「此亦難行。

translations.literal: Regulations forbade beating people to death with staffs outside the proper legal procedure; when Lushan saw this he laughed and said: "This too would be hard to carry out."
translations.idiomatic: The law forbade beating people to death with cudgels outside proper procedure; Lushan laughed when he saw it and said, "That would be hard to enforce too."

sentences.zh: 」是日，特用大杖杖死部民楊仙，坐削一官，解職。

translations.literal: That same day he specially used a large staff to beat to death a subject of his jurisdiction named Yang Xian; for this he was demoted one rank and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he took an especially heavy staff and beat to death a local subject named Yang Xian; he was stripped of one rank and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 久之，降鳳翔治中，曆原州、濟州、泗州刺史，改鄭州防禦使，遷蒲與路節度使，移臨海軍、盤安軍、寧昌軍。

translations.literal: After a long while he was demoted to administrator of Fengxiang; served successively as prefect of Yuanzhou, Jizhou, and Sizhou; was made defense commissioner of Zhengzhou; was promoted to military commissioner of the Puyu Circuit; and was transferred among the Linhai, Pan'an, and Ningchang armies.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was demoted to administrator of Fengxiang, then served as prefect of Yuan, Ji, and Si prefectures, became defense commissioner of Zhengzhou, was promoted to commissioner of the Puyu Circuit, and held commands over the Linhai, Pan'an, and Ningchang armies in turn.

sentences.zh: 貞祐二年，城破死之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyou, when the city fell he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyou, when the city was taken, he died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 蒲察合住

translations.literal: Pucha Hezhu
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Hezhu

sentences.zh: 蒲察合住，以吏起身，久為宣宗所信，聲勢烜赫，性複殘刻，人知其蠹國而莫敢言。

translations.literal: Pucha Hezhu rose from the ranks of clerks; long trusted by Emperor Xuanzong, his power and prestige blazed; his nature was moreover cruel and harsh; people knew he was ruining the state yet none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Pucha Hezhu began as a petty clerk. Long favored by Emperor Xuanzong, he wielded dazzling power; he was cruel by nature, and though everyone knew he was ruining the state, no one dared speak against him.

sentences.zh: 其子充護衛，先逐出之。

translations.literal: His son had been enrolled as a guardsman and was expelled first.
translations.idiomatic: His son, who had served as a guardsman, was expelled first.

sentences.zh: 繼而合住為恆州刺史，需次近縣。

translations.literal: Subsequently Hezhu became prefect of Hengzhou and awaited his turn in a nearby county.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhu was then appointed prefect of Heng Prefecture and waited his turn in a nearby county.

sentences.zh: 後大兵入陝西，關中震動。

translations.literal: Later, when the great army entered Shaanxi, Guanzhong was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the main Mongol forces entered Shaanxi, the Guanzhong region was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 或言合住赴恆州為北走計，朝廷命開封羈其親屬，合住出怨言曰：「殺卻我即太平矣。

translations.literal: Some said Hezhu's journey to Hengzhou was a plan to flee north; the court ordered Kaifeng to detain his family; Hezhu uttered a resentful remark: "Kill me and there will be peace at once."
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread that Hezhu was going to Hengzhou to flee north. The court ordered Kaifeng to detain his family. Hezhu complained bitterly, "Kill me and the realm will be at peace."

sentences.zh: 」尋為禦史所劾，初議笞贖，宰相以為悖理，斬於開封府門之下。

translations.literal: Soon he was impeached by the censors; at first flogging with redemption was proposed, but the chief ministers held this contrary to reason, and he was beheaded below the gate of the Kaifeng prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: Censors soon impeached him. At first the court considered flogging and a fine, but the chief ministers judged that inadequate, and he was beheaded at the gate of the Kaifeng prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 故當時有宣朝三賊之目，謂王阿裏、蒲察咬住，合住其一也。

translations.literal: Hence at the time there was the label "the three villains of the Xuan court," meaning Wang Ali, Pucha Yaozhu, and Hezhu was one of them.
translations.idiomatic: People at the time spoke of "the three villains of the Xuan court" — Wang Ali, Pucha Yaozhu, and Hezhu among them.

sentences.zh: 興定中，駙馬僕散阿海之獄，京師宣勘七十余所，阿裏輩乘時起事以肆其毒，朝士惴惴莫克自保，惟獨吉文之在開封府幕，明其不反，竟不署字，阿海誅，文之亦無所問。

translations.literal: In the Xingding era, in the case of the imperial son-in-law Pusan's Ahai, more than seventy inquisitions were announced in the capital; Ali and his kind seized the moment to act and vent their poison; court officials trembled and could not protect themselves; only Ji Wenzhi, in the staff of the Kaifeng prefecture, saw that Ahai had not rebelled and in the end refused to sign; when Ahai was executed, Wenzhi was not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xingding era, in the prosecution of the imperial son-in-law Pusan Ahai, more than seventy inquisitions were opened in the capital. Ali and his associates seized the moment to spread terror; court officials lived in fear and could not protect themselves. Only Ji Wenzhi of the Kaifeng prefectural staff, convinced that Ahai had not rebelled, refused to sign the documents. When Ahai was executed, Wenzhi was left untouched.

sentences.zh: 咬住，正大初致仕，居睢陽，潰軍變，與其家皆被殺。

translations.literal: Yaozhu retired at the beginning of the Zhengda era, lived in Suiyang, and when routed troops mutinied he and his household were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yaozhu retired early in the Zhengda era and lived in Suiyang. When mutinous routed troops rose up, he and his entire household were killed.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗喜刑罰，朝士往往被笞楚，至用刀杖決殺言者。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Xuanzong delighted in punishments; court officials were often flogged, and some who spoke out were even killed by knife or staff on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong favored harsh punishment from the start; court officials were often flogged, and some who spoke up were killed on the spot with blade or cudgel.

sentences.zh: 高琪用事，威刑自恣。

translations.literal: When Gao Qi held power, he wielded authority and punishments as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Qi held power, he used punishments as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 南渡之後，習以成風，雖士大夫亦為所移，如徒單右丞思忠好用麻椎擊人，號「麻椎相公」。

translations.literal: After the move south of the river it became a settled custom; even scholar-officials were swayed by it, as when the right vice censor-in-chief Tushan Sizhong liked to strike people with a hemp mallet and was called "Vice Censor Hemp-Mallet."
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south across the river, the habit took root; even scholar-officials caught the fever. Tushan Sizhong, the right vice censor-in-chief, liked to beat people with a hemp mallet and was nicknamed "Lord Hemp-Mallet."

sentences.zh: 李運使特立號「半截劍」，言其短小鋒利也。

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Li Teli was called "Half a Sword," meaning he was short but sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Li Teli was called "Half a Sword" — short in stature but sharp in cruelty.

sentences.zh: 馮內翰璧號「馮劊」。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Feng Bi was called "Feng the Chopper."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Feng Bi was known as "Feng the Chopper."

sentences.zh: 雷淵為禦史，至蔡州得奸豪，杖殺五百人，號曰「雷半千」。

translations.literal: Lei Yuan served as censor; when he reached Caizhou he seized local bullies and had five hundred men beaten to death, and was called "Lei Five Hundred."
translations.idiomatic: As censor, Lei Yuan went to Caizhou, seized local bullies, and had five hundred men beaten to death; he was called "Lei Five Hundred."

sentences.zh: 又有完顏麻斤出，皆以酷聞，而合住、王阿裏、李渙之徒，胥吏中尤狡刻者也。

translations.literal: There were also Wanyan Majin and others, all famed for cruelty; while Hezhu, Wang Ali, Li Huan, and their kind were the most cunning and harsh among clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Majin and others were likewise notorious for cruelty; but Hezhu, Wang Ali, Li Huan, and their like were the most cunning and vicious of all the clerks.

sentences.zh: 世之有嗜欲者，何嘗不被其害哉。

translations.literal: Those in the world who harbor desires — when have they not been harmed by them?
translations.idiomatic: Whoever in this world indulges his desires has sooner or later been ruined by them.

sentences.zh: 龍，天下之至神也，一有嗜欲，見制于人，故人君亦然。

translations.literal: The dragon is the most numinous being under Heaven; once it has a craving it is controlled by others — so it is with rulers as well.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon is the most numinous creature under Heaven; let it acquire a craving and others control it — and the same is true of rulers.

sentences.zh: 嗜欲不獨柔曼之傾意也，征伐、畋獵、土木、神仙，彼為佞者皆有以投其所好焉。

translations.literal: Cravings are not only the sway of soft beauty; campaigns, hunting, construction works, and quests for immortality — those who play the flatterer all have means to feed what their lord favors.
translations.idiomatic: Cravings are not only for soft pleasures; war, hunting, building projects, and quests for immortality — flatterers know how to feed every taste.

sentences.zh: 金主內蠱聲色，外好大喜功，莫甚于熙宗、海陵，而章宗次之。

translations.literal: The Jin rulers were inwardly beguiled by music and women and outwardly loved grand achievements; none went further than Xizong and Hailing, with Zhangzong next.
translations.idiomatic: Jin emperors were inwardly beguiled by pleasure and outwardly addicted to grand projects; none surpassed Xizong and Hailing, with Zhangzong close behind.

sentences.zh: 《金史》自蕭肄至胥持國，得佞臣之尤者七人，皆被寵遇於三君之朝，以亡其身，以蠹其國，其禍皆始於此，可不戒哉。

translations.literal: From Xiao Yi to Xu Chiguo the History of Jin records seven of the worst flatterers; all were favored in the reigns of the three rulers, lost their lives, and ruined the state — their disasters all began here. Is this not a warning?
translations.idiomatic: From Xiao Yi to Xu Chiguo, the History of Jin names seven of the worst flatterers. All won favor under those three rulers, destroyed themselves, and ruined the state — every disaster began with indulgence. Is that not a warning?

sentences.zh: 作《佞幸傳》。

translations.literal: A biography of favorites of fortune is compiled.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the compilation of the Biographies of Favorites of Fortune.

sentences.zh: 蕭肄，本奚人，有寵于熙宗，複諂事悼後，累官參知政事。

translations.literal: Xiao Yi was originally a Xi tribesman; he won favor with Emperor Xizong and again fawned on Empress Daohou, rising through repeated offices to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yi was a Xi tribesman who won favor under Emperor Xizong and fawned on Empress Daohou, rising eventually to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇統九年四月壬申夜，大風雨，雷電震壞寢殿鴟尾，有火自外入，燒內寢幃幔。

translations.literal: On the night of the ren-shen day in the fourth month of the ninth year of Huangtong, great wind and rain came; thunder and lightning shattered the owl-tail ornaments of the sleeping hall; fire entered from outside and burned the inner curtains of the sleeping quarters.
translations.idiomatic: On a stormy night in the fourth month of the ninth year of Huangtong, thunder shattered the roof ornaments of the imperial bedchamber and fire from outside set the inner curtains ablaze.

sentences.zh: 帝徙別殿避之，欲下詔罪己。

translations.literal: The emperor moved to another hall to avoid it and wished to issue an edict blaming himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor moved to another hall and wished to issue a self-reproach edict.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士張鈞視草。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Zhang Jun drafted the text.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Zhang Jun was assigned to draft it.

sentences.zh: 鈞意欲奉答天戒，當深自貶損，其文有曰：「惟德弗類，上幹天威」及「顧茲寡昧眇予小子」等語。

translations.literal: Jun intended to answer Heaven's warning with deep self-abasement; the draft contained such phrases as "my virtue is unlike [the norm], offending Heaven's majesty" and "considering my few and dim qualities, this insignificant young one."
translations.idiomatic: Jun meant to answer Heaven's warning with deep humility. His draft included such phrases as "my virtue is unlike [the norm], offending Heaven's majesty" and "considering my few and dim qualities, this insignificant young one."

sentences.zh: 肄譯奏曰：「弗類是大無道，寡者孤獨無親，昧則於人事弗曉，眇則目無所見，小子嬰孩之稱，此漢人托文字以詈主上也。

translations.literal: Yi translated and reported: "'Unlike' means greatly lacking in the Way; 'few' means alone without kin; 'dim' means not understanding human affairs; 'minute' means the eyes see nothing; 'young one' is what infants are called — these Han people use written words to revile their sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Yi translated and reported, "'Unlike' means utterly lacking in virtue; 'few' means alone and without kin; 'dim' means ignorant of affairs; 'minute' means blind; 'young one' is what one calls an infant — the Han are using written words to insult their sovereign."

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，命衛士拽鈞下殿，榜之數百，不死。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and ordered guards to drag Jun from the hall and beat him several hundred strokes; he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage, had guards drag Jun from the hall, and had him beaten hundreds of strokes — yet he did not die.

sentences.zh: 以手劍剺其口而醢之。

translations.literal: With his own hand-sword he slashed Jun's mouth and had him minced.
translations.idiomatic: With his own sword he slashed Jun's mouth and had the body minced.

sentences.zh: 賜肄通天犀帶。

translations.literal: Yi was granted a belt of heaven-piercing rhinoceros horn.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was rewarded with a belt of heaven-piercing rhinoceros horn.

sentences.zh: 憑恃恩幸，倨視同列，遂與海陵有惡。

translations.literal: Relying on imperial favor, he looked down haughtily on his peers and thus incurred Hailing's enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on imperial favor, he looked down on his peers and earned Hailing's hatred.

sentences.zh: 及篡立，加大臣官爵，例加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When he usurped the throne he raised the ranks of the great ministers; as a rule they were promoted to Silver-Green Glory Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: After usurping the throne, he raised the ranks of senior ministers, generally promoting them to Silver-Green Glory Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 數日，召肄詰之曰：「學士張鈞何罪被誅，爾何功受賞？

translations.literal: Several days later he summoned Yi and questioned him: "For what crime was Academician Zhang Jun executed, and for what merit did you receive reward?"
translations.idiomatic: A few days later he summoned Yi and demanded, "For what crime was Academician Zhang Jun executed, and for what merit did you receive a reward?"

sentences.zh: 」肄不能對。

translations.literal: Yi could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had no answer.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「朕殺汝無難事，人或以我報私怨也。

translations.literal: Hailing said: "For me to kill you would be no difficult matter; people might think I was settling a private grudge."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "Killing you would be no difficult matter — but people might think I was settling a private grudge."

sentences.zh: 」於是，詔除名，放歸田裏，禁錮不得出百里外。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict struck his name from the rolls, sent him back to his fields, and confined him so he might not go beyond a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then struck his name from office, sent him home to his fields, and confined him within a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 張仲軻

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongke
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongke

sentences.zh: 張仲軻，幼名牛兒，市井無賴，說傳奇小說，雜以俳優詼諧語為業。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongke, childhood name Niuer, was a market-town ruffian who made his living telling romance tales and adventure stories mixed with the witty banter of comic performers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongke, nicknamed "Calf" as a boy, was a market-town ruffian who earned his living telling romance tales and adventure stories laced with comic patter.

sentences.zh: 海陵引之左右，以資戲笑。

translations.literal: Hailing kept him at his side to supply amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing kept him at court for amusement.

sentences.zh: 海陵封岐國王，以為書表，及即位，為秘書郎。

translations.literal: When Hailing was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi he made Zhongke his document secretary; when he took the throne, Zhongke became a secretary of the palace library.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing was Prince of Qi he made Zhongke his document secretary; after his accession Zhongke became a secretary of the palace library.

sentences.zh: 海陵嘗對仲軻與妃嬪褻瀆，仲軻但稱死罪，不敢仰視。

translations.literal: Hailing once behaved lewdly before Zhongke with his consorts; Zhongke only cried that he deserved death and dared not look up.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing once behaved lewdly before Zhongke with his consorts; Zhongke could only cry that he deserved death and dared not look up.

sentences.zh: 又嘗令仲軻倮形以觀之，侍臣往往令倮褫，雖徒單貞亦不免此。

translations.literal: He also once ordered Zhongke to stand naked for inspection; attendants were often made to strip bare, and even Tushan Zhen was not spared.
translations.idiomatic: He once ordered Zhongke to stand naked for his inspection; attendants were often forced to strip, and even Tushan Zhen was not spared.

sentences.zh: 兵部侍郎完顏普連、大興少尹李惇皆以贓敗，海陵置之要近。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War Wanyan Pulian and Junior Administrator of Daxing Li Dun had both been ruined by bribery, yet Hailing placed them in key positions near him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War Wanyan Pulian and Junior Administrator of Daxing Li Dun had both been ruined by bribery, yet Hailing kept them in key posts at his side.

sentences.zh: 伶人于慶兒官五品、大氏家奴王之彰為秘書郎。

translations.literal: The actor Yu Qing'er was given fifth-rank office; the household slave Wang Zhizhang of the Dashi clan became a secretary of the palace library.
translations.idiomatic: The actor Yu Qing'er was given fifth-rank office; Wang Zhizhang, a slave of the Dashi household, became a palace library secretary.

sentences.zh: 之彰睾珠偏僻，海陵親視之，不以為褻。

translations.literal: Zhizhang's testicles were misshapen and protruded; Hailing personally inspected them and did not regard it as indecent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhang's testicles were misshapen and protruded; Hailing personally inspected them and saw nothing indecent in it.

sentences.zh: 唐括辯家奴和尚、烏帶家奴葛溫、葛魯，皆置宿衛，有僥倖至一品者。

translations.literal: The household slaves Heshang of Tangguo Bian's family and Gewen and Gelu of Wudai's household were all placed in the inner guard; some by favor reached first rank.
translations.idiomatic: The slaves Heshang of Tangguo Bian's household and Gewen and Gelu of Wudai's household were placed in the inner guard; some by favor rose to first rank.

sentences.zh: 左右或無官職人，或以名呼之，即授以顯階，海陵語其人曰：「爾複能名之乎？

translations.literal: Among those at his side were men without office; if he called one by name he at once granted a conspicuous rank, and Hailing would say to the man: "Can you name it again?"
translations.idiomatic: Some of those at his side held no office at all; if he called one by name he would at once grant a high rank and ask, "Can you name that rank again?"

sentences.zh: 」常置黃金茵褥間，喜之者令自取之，其濫賜如此。

translations.literal: He often placed gold among cushions and bedding; those who pleased him were told to take it themselves — such was the recklessness of his gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He often scattered gold among the cushions; those who pleased him were told to take what they wanted — such was the recklessness of his largesse.

sentences.zh: 宋余唐弼賀登寶位，且還，海陵以玉帶附賜宋帝，使謂宋帝曰：「此帶卿父所常服，今以為賜，使卿如見而父，當不忘朕意也。

translations.literal: When the Song envoy Yu Tangbi came to congratulate Hailing on taking the throne and was about to return, Hailing attached a jade belt as a gift for the Song emperor and had him told: "This belt your father often wore; I now bestow it so that, as if seeing your father, you will not forget my intent."
translations.idiomatic: When the Song envoy Yu Tangbi came to congratulate Hailing on his accession and was about to return, Hailing sent a jade belt as a gift for the Song emperor with this message: "Your father often wore this belt. I bestow it now so that, as if you saw your father again, you will not forget my goodwill."

sentences.zh: 」使退，仲軻曰：「此希世之寶，可惜輕賜。

translations.literal: When the envoy withdrew, Zhongke said: "This is a treasure rare in the world — a pity to give it away lightly."
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy withdrew, Zhongke said, "That is a treasure rare in the world — a pity to give it away so lightly."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「江南之地，他日當為我有，此置之外府耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The lands south of the Yangtze will one day be mine; this is merely stored in an outer treasury."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The lands south of the Yangtze will one day be mine; this is only stored in an outer treasury for now."

sentences.zh: 」由是知海陵有南伐之意。

translations.literal: From this it was known that Hailing intended a southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: From this people knew that Hailing intended to invade the south.

sentences.zh: 俄遷秘書丞，轉少監。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to deputy director of the palace library and then to junior director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to deputy director of the palace library, then to junior director.

sentences.zh: 是時，營建燕京宮室，有司取真定府潭園材木，仲軻乘間言其中材木不可用，海陵意仲軻受請托，免仲軻官。

translations.literal: At that time the palaces at Yanjing were under construction; the authorities took timber from the Tan Garden in Zhending Prefecture; Zhongke seized an opening to say the timber was unusable; Hailing suspected Zhongke had taken a bribe and dismissed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: While the Yanjing palaces were being built, officials took timber from the Tan Garden in Zhending Prefecture. Zhongke seized a chance to say the timber was unusable. Hailing suspected bribery and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，複用為少監。

translations.literal: Before long he was again employed as junior director.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reappointed junior director.

sentences.zh: 海陵獵於途你山，次於鐸瓦，酹天而拜，謂群臣曰：「朕幼時習射，至一門下，默祝曰：'若我異日大貴，當使一矢橫加門脊上。

translations.literal: Hailing hunted on Tuni Mountain and halted at Duowa; he poured a libation to Heaven and bowed, telling the assembled ministers: "In my youth when I practiced archery, I came to a gate and silently prayed: 'If I should one day rise to great honor, let one arrow lie across the ridge of the gate.'"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing hunted on Tuni Mountain and halted at Duowa. He poured a libation to Heaven and bowed, telling his ministers, "As a boy practicing archery I came to a gate and silently prayed: 'If I should one day rise to great honor, let one arrow lie across the ridge of the gate.'"

sentences.zh: '及射，果橫加門脊上。

translations.literal: When he shot, the arrow indeed lay across the ridge of the gate.
translations.idiomatic: When he shot, the arrow indeed lay across the ridge of the gate.

sentences.zh: 後為中京留守，嘗大獵於此地，圍未合，禱曰：'我若有大位，百步之內當獲三鹿。

translations.literal: Later, as military commissioner of the Central Capital, he once held a great hunt in this place; before the beaters had closed the ring he prayed: 'If I am to attain high rank, within a hundred paces I shall take three deer.'
translations.idiomatic: Later, as commissioner of the Central Capital, he held a great hunt here. Before the beaters closed the ring he prayed, 'If I am to attain high rank, I shall take three deer within a hundred paces.'

sentences.zh: 若止為公相，獲一而已。

translations.literal: If I were only to become a chief minister, I would take but one.
translations.idiomatic: If I were only to become a chief minister, I would take but one.

sentences.zh: '於是不及百步連獲三鹿。

translations.literal: Before a hundred paces he took three deer in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before a hundred paces he took three deer in succession.

sentences.zh: 又祝曰：'若統一海內，當複獲一大鹿。

translations.literal: He prayed again: 'If I unite the realm within the Four Seas, I shall again take one great deer.'
translations.idiomatic: He prayed again, 'If I unite the realm within the Four Seas, I shall again take one great deer.'

sentences.zh: ' 於是果獲一大鹿。

translations.literal: And indeed he took one great deer.
translations.idiomatic: And indeed he took one great deer.

sentences.zh: 此事嘗與蕭裕言之，朕今複至此地，故拜奠焉。

translations.literal: I once spoke of this matter to Xiao Yu; I have now come again to this place, and therefore offer worship and libation.
translations.idiomatic: I once told Xiao Yu of this; I have come again to this place, and so I offer worship and libation.

sentences.zh: 」海陵意欲取江南，故先設禨祥以諷群臣，是以仲軻每先逢其意，導之南伐。

translations.literal: Hailing intended to seize the lands south of the Yangtze; he therefore first staged auspicious signs to admonish the ministers — hence Zhongke always anticipated his intent and guided him toward the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing intended to seize the south. He staged auspicious signs to sway his ministers, and Zhongke always anticipated his intent and urged the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年正月，宋賀正旦使施巨朝辭，海陵使左宣徽使敬嗣暉問施巨曰：「宋國幾科取士？

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Zhenyuan, when the Song envoy for New Year's congratulations Shi Ju took leave at court, Hailing had the Left Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat Jing Sihui ask Shi Ju: "In how many examination categories does the Song state select scholars?"
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Zhenyuan, when the Song New Year's envoy Shi Ju took leave at court, Hailing had Left Commissioner Jing Sihui ask him, "In how many examination categories does the Song state select scholars?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「詩賦、經義、策論兼行。

translations.literal: He answered: "Poetry and rhapsody, classical exegesis, and policy essays are all used together."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Poetry and rhapsody, classical exegesis, and policy essays are all used together."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「秦檜作何官，年今幾何？

translations.literal: He asked again: "What office does Qin Hui hold, and how old is he now?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "What office does Qin Hui hold, and how old is he now?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「檜為尚書左僕射中書門下平章事，年六十五矣。

translations.literal: He answered: "Hui is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery; he is sixty-five."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Hui is Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Grand Councilor; he is sixty-five."

sentences.zh: 」複謂之曰：「我聞秦檜賢，故問之。」

translations.literal: He further told him: "I have heard Qin Hui is worthy, and therefore asked."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I have heard Qin Hui is a worthy man — that is why I asked."

sentences.zh: 正隆二年，仲軻為左諫議大夫，修起居注，但食諫議俸，不得言事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenglong, Zhongke became Left Remonstrance Grand Master and compiled the diary of conduct, but received only the Remonstrance salary and was not permitted to speak on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenglong, Zhongke became Left Remonstrance Grand Master and compiled the imperial diary, but received only the remonstrance salary and was not allowed to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，宋賀正使孫道夫陛辭，海陵使左宣徽使敬嗣暉諭之曰：「歸白爾帝，事我上國多有不誠，今略舉二事：爾民有逃入我境者，邊吏皆即發還，我民有逃叛入爾境者，有司索之往往託辭不發，一也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, when the Song New Year's envoy Sun Daofu took leave at court, Hailing had Jing Sihui instruct him: "Return and tell your emperor: in dealings with our state you have often been insincere. I will cite two matters briefly. When your people flee into our territory, border officials at once send them back; when our people flee in rebellion into your territory, your authorities, when asked for them, often make excuses and do not surrender them — the first matter."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year, when the Song New Year's envoy Sun Daofu took leave, Hailing had Jing Sihui instruct him, "Tell your emperor: in dealings with our state you have often been insincere. I cite two examples. When your people flee into our territory, our border officials send them back at once; when our people flee into yours, your authorities make excuses and refuse to return them — the first matter."

sentences.zh: 爾於沿邊盜買鞍馬，備戰陣，二也。

translations.literal: You secretly buy saddles and horses along the border to prepare battle arrays — the second matter.
translations.idiomatic: You secretly buy saddles and horses along the border to prepare for war — the second matter.

sentences.zh: 且馬待人而後可用，如無其人，得馬百萬亦奚以為？

translations.literal: Moreover, horses wait upon men before they can be used; without such men, even a million horses — of what use would they be?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, horses are useless without men to ride them; a million horses are worthless if you lack the riders.

sentences.zh: 我亦豈能無備。

translations.literal: Can I too be without preparations?
translations.idiomatic: Do you think we are unprepared?

sentences.zh: 且我不取爾國則已，如欲取之，固非難事。

translations.literal: Moreover, if I do not take your state, so be it; if I wish to take it, that is surely no difficult matter.
translations.idiomatic: If I choose not to take your state, so be it; if I wish to take it, that will not be difficult.

sentences.zh: 我聞接納叛亡、盜買鞍馬，皆爾國楊太尉所為，常因俘獲問知其人，無能為者也。

translations.literal: I have heard that receiving defectors and secretly buying saddles and horses are all the doing of your state's Grand Marshal Yang; I have often learned of this man through captives — he is incapable of anything.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that receiving defectors and buying horses on the sly are the work of your Grand Marshal Yang. Captives have told me about him — he is no threat.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「聞秦檜已死，果否？

translations.literal: He said again: "I have heard Qin Hui is already dead — is it true?"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "I have heard Qin Hui is dead — is it true?"

sentences.zh: 」道夫對曰：「檜實死矣，陪臣亦檜所薦用者。

translations.literal: Daofu answered: "Hui is indeed dead; your humble servant was also one whom Hui recommended for appointment."
translations.idiomatic: Daofu answered, "Hui is indeed dead — and I myself was recommended by him."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「爾國比來行事，殊不似秦檜時何也？

translations.literal: He said again: "Your state's conduct of late is quite unlike the time of Qin Hui — why?"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Your state's conduct of late is nothing like the Qin Hui era — why is that?"

sentences.zh: 」道夫曰：「容陪臣還國，一一具聞宋帝。

translations.literal: Daofu said: "Allow your humble servant to return to my state and report each matter in full to the Song emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Daofu said, "Let me return home and lay out each of your points before the Song emperor."

sentences.zh: 」海陵蓋欲南伐，故先設納叛亡、盜買馬二事，而雜以他辭言之。

translations.literal: Hailing in fact intended a southern campaign; he therefore first set up the two matters of receiving defectors and secretly buying horses, and spoke of them mixed with other words.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was already bent on invading the south; he had planted those two charges—harboring defectors and illicit horse-buying—then woven them into talk of other things.

sentences.zh: 海陵召仲軻、右補闕馬欽、校書郎田與信、直長習失入便殿侍坐。

translations.literal: Hailing summoned Zhongke, Right Supplementation Censor Ma Qin, Collator Tian Yuxin, and Regular Attendant Xishi to enter the privy chamber and sit in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing called in Zhongke, the Right Supplementation Censor Ma Qin, the Collator Tian Yuxin, and the Regular Attendant Xishi to wait on him in the privy chamber.

sentences.zh: 海陵與仲軻論《漢書》，謂仲軻曰：「漢之封疆不過七八千里，今吾國幅員萬里，可謂大矣。

translations.literal: Hailing discussed the Book of Han with Zhongke and said to Zhongke: "Han territory extended no more than seven or eight thousand li; today our state's breadth spans ten thousand li — it may be called great."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was discussing the Book of Han with Zhongke and said, "The Han domains stretched only seven or eight thousand li; our realm spans ten thousand li today—surely that is greatness."

sentences.zh: 」仲軻曰：「本朝疆土雖大，而天下有四主，南有宋，東有高麗，西有夏，若能一之，乃為大耳。

translations.literal: Zhongke said: "Though our dynasty's territory is large, under Heaven there are four rulers: to the south Song, to the east Goryeo, to the west Xia — only if these can be made one is it truly great."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongke said, "Our lands are vast, but the world still has four sovereigns—Song in the south, Goryeo in the east, Xia in the west. True greatness would be to unite them."

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「彼且何罪而伐之？

translations.literal: Hailing said: "What crime have they committed that I should attack them?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing asked, "What have they done wrong that I should attack them?"

sentences.zh: 」仲軻曰：「臣聞宋人買馬修器械，招納山東叛亡，豈得為無罪？

translations.literal: Zhongke said: "Your servant has heard that the Song buy horses and repair weapons, and receive defectors from east of the mountains — how can that be called no crime?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhongke said, "I hear the Song are buying horses, readying arms, and taking in defectors from Shandong—how can that be no offense?"

sentences.zh: 」海陵喜曰：「向者梁珫嘗為朕言，宋有劉貴妃者姿質豔美，蜀之華蕊、吳之西施所不及也。

translations.literal: Hailing said with pleasure: "Formerly Liang Guan once told Us that in Song there is a Noble Consort Liu of surpassing beauty — Shu's Huarui and Wu's Xishi cannot equal her."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing brightened. "Liang Guan once told me the Song have a Noble Consort Liu of extraordinary beauty—Shu's Huarui and Wu's Xishi are nothing beside her."

sentences.zh: 今一舉而兩得之，俗所謂'因行掉手'也。

translations.literal: Now with one stroke two gains are obtained — what the common saying calls 'picking up something extra while you're at it.'
translations.idiomatic: One campaign and I win both—what people call getting a bonus on the way.

sentences.zh: 江南聞我舉兵，必遠竄耳。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan hears that I am raising troops, they will surely flee far away.
translations.idiomatic: When the south hears I am marching, they will run for the ends of the earth.

sentences.zh: 」欽與與信俱對曰：「海島、蠻越，臣等皆知道路，彼將安往？

translations.literal: Qin and Yuxin together replied: "To sea-islands and the lands of the southern barbarians — we all know the roads; where could they go?"
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Yuxin answered together, "Sea islands, barbarian coasts—we know every road. Where could they flee?"

sentences.zh: 」欽又曰：「臣在宋時，嘗帥軍征蠻，所以知也。

translations.literal: Qin also said: "When your servant was in Song, I once led troops to campaign against the barbarians — that is how I know."
translations.idiomatic: Qin added, "When I served in Song I led campaigns against the southern tribes—that is how I know."

sentences.zh: 」海陵謂習失曰：「汝敢戰乎？

translations.literal: Hailing said to Xishi: "Do you dare fight?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing turned to Xishi. "Would you dare fight?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「受恩日久，死亦何避。

translations.literal: He replied: "Having received favor for long, even death — what is there to avoid?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "You have favored me for years; I would not shrink from death."

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「汝料彼敢出兵否，彼若出兵，汝果能死敵乎？

translations.literal: Hailing said: "Do you reckon they will dare send out troops? If they send out troops, can you in truth fight to the death against the enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "Do you think they will dare march out? If they do, will you truly stand and die against them?"

sentences.zh: 」習失良久曰：「臣雖懦弱，亦將與之為敵矣。

translations.literal: After a long while Xishi said: "Though your servant is timid, I too shall become their enemy."
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause Xishi said, "Timid as I am, I would still face them as an enemy."

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「彼將出兵何地？

translations.literal: Hailing said: "From where will they send out troops?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing asked, "Where would they march out from?"

sentences.zh: 」曰：「不過淮上耳。

translations.literal: He said: "Nothing beyond the Huai, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Nowhere but the Huai line."

sentences.zh: 」海陵曰：「然則天與我也。

translations.literal: Hailing said: "Then Heaven has given it to me."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "Then Heaven has handed it to me."

sentences.zh: 」既而曰：「朕舉兵滅宋，遠不過二三年，然後討平高麗、夏國。

translations.literal: Presently he said: "When I raise troops to destroy Song, it will be at most two or three years; afterward I shall pacify Goryeo and the Xia state."
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "When I march to destroy Song it will take at most two or three years; then I will subdue Goryeo and Xia."

sentences.zh: 一統之後，論功遷秩，分賞將士，彼必忘勞矣。」

translations.literal: After unification, by merit offices and ranks will be advanced, rewards divided among generals and soldiers — they will surely forget their toil."
translations.idiomatic: After the realm is one, I will promote by merit and reward officers and men—they will forget their hardships."

sentences.zh: 四年三月，仲軻死。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year, Zhongke died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year, Zhongke died.

sentences.zh: 冬至前一夕，海陵夢仲軻求酒，既覺，嗟悼良久，遣使者奠其墓。

translations.literal: On the eve before the winter solstice, Hailing dreamed that Zhongke begged for wine; when he awoke, he sighed in mourning for a long while and sent an envoy to offer libation at his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On the night before the winter solstice Hailing dreamed Zhongke begging for wine. When he woke he mourned at length and sent an envoy to pour offerings at his grave.

sentences.zh: 李通，以便辟側媚得幸於海陵。

translations.literal: Li Tong, through clever compliance and ingratiating flattery, won Hailing's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tong won Hailing's favor through clever compliance and ingratiating flattery.

sentences.zh: 累官右司郎中，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: By successive offices he reached Right Department Director; he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Right Department Director, then was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 請謁賄賂輻輳其門。

translations.literal: Requests for audience and bribes converged thickly at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Petitioners and bribes crowded his gate.

sentences.zh: 正隆二年正月乙酉，詔左右司禦史中丞以下奏事便殿，海陵曰：「知子莫若父，知臣莫若君，朕嘗試之矣。

translations.literal: On yiyou of the first month of the second year of Zhenglong, an edict ordered those from the Left and Right Departments and the Censor-in-Chief downward to memorialize at the privy chamber; Hailing said: "No one knows a son like a father, no one knows a minister like a ruler — I have put this to the test."
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou of the first month of Zhenglong 2, an edict summoned officials from the Left and Right Departments and the Censor-in-Chief down to report at the privy chamber. Hailing said, "No one knows a son like his father, no one knows a minister like his lord—I have tested that."

sentences.zh: 朕詢及人材，汝等若不舉同類，必舉其相善者。

translations.literal: When I inquired about talent, if you did not recommend your own kind, you surely recommended those on good terms with you.
translations.idiomatic: When I asked about talent, you either recommended your own kind or your friends.

sentences.zh: 朕聞女直、契丹之仕進者，必賴刑部尚書烏帶、簽書樞密遙設為之先容，左司員外郎阿裏骨列任其事。

translations.literal: I have heard that Jurchen and Khitan who sought advancement all relied on Minister of Justice Wudai and Privy Council Deputy Yaoshe to introduce them first, while Left Department Vice Director Aligulie handled the matter.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Jurchen and Khitan seeking office all needed Minister of Justice Wudai and Privy Council Deputy Yaoshe to speak for them first, with Left Department Vice Director Aligulie handling the paperwork.

sentences.zh: 渤海、漢人仕進者，必賴吏部尚書李通、戶部尚書許霖為之先容，左司郎中王蔚任其事。

translations.literal: Bohai and Han who sought advancement all relied on Minister of Personnel Li Tong and Minister of Revenue Xu Lin to introduce them first, while Left Department Director Wang Wei handled the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Bohai and Han seeking office relied on Li Tong at Personnel and Xu Lin at Revenue for introductions, with Left Department Director Wang Wei running the process.

sentences.zh: 凡在仕版，朕識者寡，不識者眾，莫非人臣，豈有遠近親疏之異哉。

translations.literal: Of all on the roster of office, few do I know, many I do not — yet are they not all ministers? How could there be difference of near and far, kin and stranger?
translations.idiomatic: Of everyone in office I know few and do not know many—yet are they not all my ministers? Why should nearness or kinship matter?

sentences.zh: 苟奉職無愆，尚書侍郎節度使便可得，萬一獲罪，必罰無赦。

translations.literal: If you fulfill your duties without fault, minister, vice-minister, or military commissioner may be obtained; if by any chance you incur guilt, punishment will surely be without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Serve without fault and you may reach minister, vice-minister, or commissioner; commit an offense and punishment will be merciless.

sentences.zh: 」頃之，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, he was appointed Vice Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Vice Councilor.

sentences.zh: 海陵恃累世強盛，欲大肆征伐，以一天下，嘗曰：「天下一家，然後可以為正統。

translations.literal: Hailing relied on generations of strength and wished to campaign on a great scale to unify the realm under Heaven; he once said: "Only when all under Heaven is one family may one be called orthodox succession."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing, trusting in generations of power, meant to wage war on a vast scale and unite the realm. He once said, "Only when the world is one family can rule be called orthodox."

sentences.zh: 」通揣知其意，遂與張仲軻、馬欽、宦者梁珫近習群小輩，盛談江南富庶，子女玉帛之多，逢其意而先道之。

translations.literal: Tong divined his intent and thereupon, together with Zhang Zhongke, Ma Qin, the eunuch Liang Guan, and the crowd of intimate petty men, spoke at length of Jiangnan's wealth and abundance of sons and daughters, jade and silks, meeting his intent and speaking of it first.
translations.idiomatic: Tong read his mind and, with Zhang Zhongke, Ma Qin, the eunuch Liang Guan, and other court favorites, lavished talk on Jiangnan's wealth—its people, its jade and silk—getting ahead of his desire and saying it first.

sentences.zh: 海陵信其言，以通為謀主，遂議興兵伐江南。

translations.literal: Hailing believed their words, made Tong chief strategist, and thereupon deliberated raising troops to attack Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing believed them, made Tong his chief strategist, and began planning war against the south.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，海陵諭宰相曰「宋國雖臣服，有誓約而無誠實，比聞沿邊買馬及招納叛亡，不可不備。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, Hailing instructed the chief ministers: "Though the Song state has submitted, there are sworn covenants but no sincerity; recently I have heard of buying horses along the border and receiving defectors — this cannot go unprepared for."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year Hailing told the chief ministers, "Song may bow, but their oaths are hollow; I hear they are buying horses on the border and taking defectors—we must prepare."

sentences.zh: 」遣使籍諸路猛安部族、及州縣渤海丁莊充軍，仍括諸道民馬。

translations.literal: He dispatched envoys to register the meng'an tribes of all circuits and Bohai households in prefectures and counties for military service, and also to requisition civilian horses on all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to register meng'an tribes and Bohai households in every prefecture and county for service, and to seize civilian horses on every circuit.

sentences.zh: 於是，遣使分往上京、速頻路、胡裏改路、曷懶路、蒲與路、泰州、咸平府、東京、婆速路、曷蘇館、臨潢府、西南招討司、西北招討司、北京、河間府、真定府、益都府、東平府、大名府、西京路，凡年二十以上、五十以下者皆籍之，雖親老丁多，求一子留侍，亦不聽，五年十一月，使益都尹京等三十一人押諸路軍器於軍行要會處安置，俟軍至分給之。

translations.literal: Thereupon envoys were sent separately to Shangjing, Supin Circuit, Huligai Circuit, Helan Circuit, Puyu Circuit, Taizhou, Xianping Prefecture, Dongjing, Basu Circuit, Hesuguan, Linhuang Prefecture, the Southwest Pacification Commission, the Northwest Pacification Commission, Beijing, Hejian Prefecture, Zhending Prefecture, Yidu Prefecture, Dongping Prefecture, Daming Prefecture, and Xijing Circuit; all from twenty years of age up to fifty were registered. Though parents were old and sons many, a request to leave one son to attend them was not granted. In the eleventh month of the fifth year, Yidu Prefect Yin Jing and thirty others were sent to escort military equipment of all circuits to the army's rendezvous points for placement, to be distributed when the army arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were then dispatched across Shangjing, Supin, Huligai, Helan, Puyu, Taizhou, Xianping, Dongjing, Basu, Hesuguan, Linhuang, the southwest and northwest pacification commissions, Beijing, Hejian, Zhending, Yidu, Dongping, Daming, and Xijing Circuit to register every man from twenty to fifty. Even families with aged parents and many sons were denied a single son left at home. In the eleventh month of the fifth year Yin Jing, prefect of Yidu, and thirty others were ordered to convoy weapons from every circuit to the army's staging points for issue when the troops arrived.

sentences.zh: 其分給之餘與繕完不及者，皆聚而焚之。

translations.literal: What remained after distribution and what could not be repaired in time were all gathered and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus stores and gear that could not be repaired in time were heaped up and burned.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，海陵使通諭旨宋使徐度等曰：「朕昔從梁王嘗居南京，樂其風土。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year, Hailing had Tong convey his intent to the Song envoys Xu Du and others, saying: "In former days I followed Prince Liang and once dwelt at Nanjing, and delighted in its winds and soil."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year Hailing had Tong tell the Song envoys Xu Du and others, "I once followed Prince Liang and lived at Nanjing; I loved its country."

sentences.zh: 帝王巡狩，自古有之。

translations.literal: Imperial tours of inspection have existed since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial tours are as old as kingship.

sentences.zh: 淮右多隙地，欲校獵其間，從兵不逾萬人。

translations.literal: South of the Huai there is much vacant land; I wish to hunt there between them, with escort troops not exceeding ten thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: There is open country south of the Huai where I wish to hunt; my escort will not exceed ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 汝等歸告汝主，令有司宣諭朕意，使淮南之民無懷疑懼。

translations.literal: You and the rest return and tell your lord; let the responsible offices proclaim My intent, so that the people of Huainan harbor no doubt or fear.
translations.idiomatic: Go back and tell your emperor; let his officials announce my intent so the people of Huainan need not fear.

sentences.zh: 」二月，通進拜右丞，詔曰：「卿典領繕完兵械，今已畢功，朕嘉卿忠謹，故有是命，俟江南事畢，別當旌賞。」

translations.literal: In the second month, Tong was advanced to Right Vice Chancellor; the edict said: "You have overseen the repair of weapons and armor; now the work is finished. I commend your loyalty and prudence, hence this appointment; when the Jiangnan affair is concluded, separate rewards and distinctions will be granted."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Tong was promoted Right Vice Chancellor. The edict read, "You have overseen arms and armor to completion; I reward your loyalty with this post. When the southern campaign ends, further honors will follow."

sentences.zh: 四月，簽書樞密院事高景山為賜宋帝生日使，右司員外郎王全副之，海陵謂全曰：「汝見宋主，即面數其焚南京宮室、沿邊買馬、招致叛亡之罪，當令大臣某人某人來此，朕將親詰問之，且索漢、淮之地，如不從，即厲聲詆責之，彼必不敢害汝。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Privy Council Deputy Gao Jingshan was made envoy for the Song emperor's birthday, with Right Department Vice Director Wang Quan as deputy; Hailing said to Quan: "When you see the Song ruler, at once face him and count out his crimes of burning the Nanjing palaces, buying horses along the border, and drawing in defectors; certain ministers such-and-such must come here — I shall personally interrogate them; moreover demand the lands of Han and Huai; if they do not comply, then revile them in a harsh voice — they will surely not dare harm you."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Privy Council Deputy Gao Jingshan was sent as birthday envoy to the Song emperor, with Right Department Vice Director Wang Quan as deputy. Hailing told Quan, "When you see the Song ruler, accuse him to his face of burning the Nanjing palaces, buying horses on the border, and harboring defectors. Demand that such-and-such ministers come here for me to question myself, and claim the Han and Huai lands. If he refuses, berate him loudly—they will not dare touch you."

sentences.zh: 」海陵蓋使王全激怒宋主，將以為南伐之名也。

translations.literal: Hailing in fact meant to have Wang Quan enrage the Song ruler, taking that as a name for the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing meant Quan to provoke the Song emperor and supply a pretext for invasion.

sentences.zh: 謂景山曰：「回日，以全所言奏聞。

translations.literal: He said to Jingshan: "On your return, memorialize what Quan said."
translations.idiomatic: He told Jingshan, "On your return, report everything Quan said."

sentences.zh: 」全至宋，一如海陵之言詆責宋主，宋主謂全曰：「聞公北方名家，何乃如是？

translations.literal: Quan reached Song and, just as Hailing had said, reviled the Song ruler; the Song ruler said to Quan: "I hear you are of a famous northern house — how can you be like this?"
translations.idiomatic: Quan reached Song and abused the emperor exactly as Hailing had instructed. The Song ruler said, "They say you come from a great northern house—how can you behave like this?"

sentences.zh: 」全複曰：「趙桓今已死矣。

translations.literal: Quan replied again: "Zhao Huan is already dead."
translations.idiomatic: Quan shot back, "Zhao Huan is dead already."

sentences.zh: 」宋主遽起發哀而罷。

translations.literal: The Song ruler abruptly rose, began mourning, and the audience ended.
translations.idiomatic: The Song ruler sprang up, broke into mourning, and the audience ended.

sentences.zh: 海陵至南京，宋遣使賀遷都，海陵使韓汝嘉就境上止之曰：「朕始至此，比聞北方小警，欲複歸中都，無庸來賀。

translations.literal: When Hailing reached Nanjing, Song dispatched envoys to congratulate the move of the capital; Hailing had Han Rujia go to the border to stop them, saying: "I have only just arrived here; I have lately heard small alarms in the north and wish to return to the central capital — there is no need to come congratulate."
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing reached Nanjing the Song sent envoys to congratulate his move of the capital. He had Han Rujia meet them at the border and say, "I have only just arrived; I hear of trouble in the north and may return to the central capital—no need to congratulate."

sentences.zh: 」宋使乃還。

translations.literal: The Song envoys thereupon returned.
translations.idiomatic: The Song envoys turned back.

sentences.zh: 於是，大括天下騾馬，官至七品聽留一馬，等而上之。

translations.literal: Thereupon mules and horses were requisitioned on a grand scale throughout the realm; officials of the seventh rank were permitted to keep one horse, and so upward by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Then the court seized mules and horses empire-wide; officials of seventh rank and above might keep one horse, with more allowed by higher rank.

sentences.zh: 並舊籍民馬，其在東者給西軍，在西者給東軍，東西交相往來，晝夜絡繹不絕，死者狼籍于道。

translations.literal: Together with civilian horses on the old registers, those in the east were given to western armies and those in the west to eastern armies; east and west crossed back and forth, day and night in unbroken stream, the dead heaped along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Registered civilian horses in the east went to western armies and western horses to eastern ones; convoys crossed day and night without pause, and the dead littered the roads.

sentences.zh: 其亡失多者，官吏懼罪或自殺。

translations.literal: Where many were lost on the way, officials fearing guilt sometimes killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who lost too many animals, fearing punishment, sometimes took their own lives.

sentences.zh: 所過蹂踐民田，調發牽馬夫役。

translations.literal: Where they passed they trampled the people's fields and requisitioned men to lead horses and perform corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Convoys trampled fields and pressed men into service as horse handlers and laborers.

sentences.zh: 詔河南州縣所貯糧米以備大軍，不得他用，而騾馬所至當給芻粟，無可給，有司以為請，海陵曰：「此方比歲民間儲畜尚多，今禾稼滿野，騾馬可就牧田中，借令再歲不獲，亦何傷乎。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the grain stored in Henan prefectures and counties to be reserved for the great army and not used otherwise; yet wherever mules and horses arrived fodder and grain had to be supplied, and when there was none to give, the offices memorialized; Hailing said: "In this region in recent years the people's stored goods are still plentiful; now the grain stands full in the fields — the mules and horses may be pastured in the standing crop; even if for two years there were no harvest, what harm would there be?"
translations.idiomatic: An edict reserved Henan's stored grain for the main army alone. Wherever convoys passed they had to be fed; when stores ran out officials appealed. Hailing said, "This region still has plenty in the barns, and the fields are full—let the animals graze the standing grain. Even two years without harvest would do no harm."

sentences.zh: 」及徵發諸道工匠至京師，疫死者不可勝數，天下始騷然矣。

translations.literal: When craftsmen of all circuits were conscripted to the capital, those who died of pestilence could not be counted; all under Heaven began to be in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: When craftsmen were summoned from every circuit to the capital, plague killed untold numbers, and the realm began to boil.

sentences.zh: 調諸路馬以戶口為率，富室有至六十匹者。

translations.literal: Horses of all circuits were requisitioned according to household registers; wealthy households had as many as sixty head.
translations.idiomatic: Horses were levied by household count; rich families surrendered as many as sixty.

sentences.zh: 凡調馬五十六萬餘匹，仍令本家養飼，以俟師期。

translations.literal: In all, more than five hundred sixty thousand horses were requisitioned; households were still ordered to feed and keep them, awaiting the date of the army.
translations.idiomatic: More than five hundred sixty thousand horses were levied, yet each household had to feed them until the army marched.

sentences.zh: 海陵因出獵，遂至通州觀造戰船，籍諸路水手得三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Hailing went out hunting and thereupon reached Tongzhou to inspect the building of warships; sailors of all circuits were registered, obtaining more than thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunting excursion Hailing went to Tongzhou to inspect warship construction and registered more than thirty thousand sailors from every circuit.

sentences.zh: 及東海縣人張旺、徐元反，遣都水監徐文等率師浮海討之，海陵曰：「朕意不在一邑，將試舟師耳。

translations.literal: When Zhang Wang and Xu Yuan of Donghai County rebelled, he dispatched the Directorate of Waterways Xu Wen and others to lead troops by sea to suppress them; Hailing said: "My intent is not in one district — I mean to test the fleet."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Wang and Xu Yuan rebelled in Donghai County he sent Xu Wen of the Directorate of Waterways with a fleet to crush them. Hailing said, "I care nothing for one county—I am testing the navy."

sentences.zh: 」於是民不堪命，盜賊蜂起，大者連城邑，小者保山澤，遣護衛普連二十四人，各授甲士五十人，分往山東、河北、河東、中都等路節鎮州郡屯駐，捕捉盜賊。

translations.literal: Thereupon the people could not bear their orders; bandits rose in swarms — the great joining whole cities and towns, the small holding mountains and marshes. He dispatched twenty-four Imperial Guards, Puchain and others, each given fifty armored soldiers, separately sent to garrison in the circuits of Shandong, Hebei, Hedong, and Zhongdu and in the military commissioners' prefectures and counties to capture bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The people could endure no more; rebels swarmed—large bands seizing cities, small bands holding hills and marshes. He sent twenty-four Imperial Guards, including Puchain, each with fifty armored men, to garrison Shandong, Hebei, Hedong, Zhongdu, and other circuits and hunt bandits.

sentences.zh: 以護衛頑犀為定武軍節度副使，尚賢為安武軍節度副使，蒲甲為昭義軍節度副使，皆給銀牌，使督責之。

translations.literal: Imperial Guard Wanxi was made Military Commissioner Deputy of Dingwu Army, Shangxian Deputy of Anwu Army, and Puja Deputy of Zhaoyi Army — all were given silver plaques and sent to press and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Wanxi was made deputy commissioner of Dingwu, Shangxian of Anwu, and Puja of Zhaoyi; each received a silver plaque and orders to drive the hunt.

sentences.zh: 是時，山東賊犯沂州，臨沂令胡撒力戰而死。

translations.literal: At this time Shandong bandits attacked Yizhou; Linyi magistrate Hu Sa fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits in Shandong struck Yizhou; the magistrate of Linyi, Hu Sa, died fighting.

sentences.zh: 大名府賊王九等據城叛，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: At Daming Prefecture the bandit Wang Jiu and others seized the city in rebellion; their host reached tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At Daming, Wang Jiu and others seized the city; their force numbered tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 契丹邊六斤、王三輩皆以十數騎張旗幟，白晝公行，官軍不敢誰何，所過州縣，開劫府庫物置於市，令人攘取之，小人皆喜賊至，而良民不勝其害。

translations.literal: Khitan on the border such as Bianliujin and Wang San and their kind, each with a dozen horsemen flying banners, marched openly by day; government troops did not dare challenge them. In every prefecture and county they passed they broke open treasuries and set goods in the market for people to snatch; the lowly all rejoiced when bandits came, while good people could not bear the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan raiders such as Bianliujin and Wang San rode openly by day with a dozen men and banners; troops dared not stop them. They looted treasuries and piled goods in markets for the crowd to seize; the poor welcomed the bandits while the law-abiding suffered.

sentences.zh: 太府監高彥福、大理正耶律道、翰林待制大穎出使還朝，皆言盜賊事。

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Imperial Storehouse Gao Yanfu, Senior Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Yelü Dao, and Hanlin Attendant Drafter Da Ying, returning from missions abroad, all spoke of bandit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yanfu of the Imperial Storehouse, Yelü Dao of the Court of Review, and Hanlin attendant Da Ying, returning from missions, all reported on the bandits.

sentences.zh: 海陵惡聞，怒而杖之，穎仍除名，自是人人不復敢言。

translations.literal: Hailing hated to hear it; in anger he had them beaten with the staff; Da Ying was still removed from office — from then on no one again dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing hated such news, had them beaten, and struck Da Ying from the rolls; after that no one dared speak.

sentences.zh: 海陵自將，分諸道兵為神策、神威、神捷、神銳、神毅、神翼、神勇、神果、神略、神鋒、武勝、武定、武威、武安、武捷、武平、武成、武毅、武銳、武揚、武翼、武震、威定、威信、威勝、威捷、威烈、威毅、威震、威略、威果、威勇三十二軍，置都總管、副總管各一員，分隸左右領軍大都督及三道都統制府。

translations.literal: Hailing himself took command, dividing troops of all circuits into thirty-two armies: Divine Strategy, Divine Might, Divine Swiftness, Divine Sharpness, Divine Perseverance, Divine Wings, Divine Courage, Divine Fruit, Divine Design, Divine Edge, Martial Victory, Martial Stability, Martial Prestige, Martial Peace, Martial Swiftness, Martial Completion, Martial Perseverance, Martial Sharpness, Martial Exaltation, Martial Wings, Martial Quake, Prestige Stability, Prestige Faith, Prestige Victory, Prestige Swiftness, Prestige Fierceness, Prestige Perseverance, Prestige Quake, Prestige Design, Prestige Fruit, Prestige Courage — establishing for each one Chief Commander and Deputy Commander, each subordinated to the Left and Right Frontier Grand Marshals and the three Circuit Grand Command Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing took personal command and divided forces from every circuit into thirty-two armies—Divine Strategy, Divine Might, Divine Swiftness, Divine Sharpness, Divine Perseverance, Divine Wings, Divine Courage, Divine Fruit, Divine Design, Divine Edge, and the Martial and Prestige series—each with a chief and deputy commander under the left and right frontier marshals and the three grand command offices.

sentences.zh: 置諸軍巡察使、副各一員。

translations.literal: For all armies an Inspector and Deputy Inspector were established.
translations.idiomatic: Each army received an inspector and deputy inspector.

sentences.zh: 乙太保奔睹為左領軍大提督，通為副大都督。

translations.literal: Yitaibao Benzhe was made Left Frontier Grand Marshal, Tong Deputy Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Yitaibao Benzhe became Left Frontier Grand Marshal; Tong became deputy grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 海陵以奔睹舊將，使帥諸軍以從人望，實使通專其事。

translations.literal: Hailing, because Benzhe was an old general, had him command the armies to follow men's expectations, but in fact let Tong monopolize the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Because Benzhe was a veteran general Hailing put him at the head of the armies to satisfy expectation, but Tong in fact ran everything.

sentences.zh: 海陵召諸將授方略，賜宴於尚書省。

translations.literal: Hailing summoned the generals and handed down strategy, granting a feast at the Ministry of State.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing summoned his generals, issued strategy, and feasted them at the Ministry of State.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「太師梁王連年南伐，淹延歲月。

translations.literal: Hailing said: "Grand Marshal Liang's southern campaigns year after year dragged on for months."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "Grand Marshal Liang's southern campaigns dragged on for months year after year."

sentences.zh: 今舉兵必不如彼，遠則百日，近止旬月。

translations.literal: Today's raising of troops will surely not be like that; at farthest a hundred days, at nearest only a ten-day month.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign will not be like his—at most a hundred days, at least a fortnight.

sentences.zh: 惟爾將士無以征行為勞，戮力一心，以成大功，當厚加旌賞，其或弛慢，刑茲無赦。

translations.literal: Only you generals and soldiers — do not take the campaign march as toil; exert your strength with one heart to accomplish the great achievement; generous rewards and distinctions will be added; if any are slack, punishment upon them will be without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Do not complain of the march; with one heart win the great victory and I will reward you richly. Slackness will be punished without mercy.

sentences.zh: 」海陵恐糧運不繼，命諸軍渡江無以僮僕從行，聞者莫不怨咨。

translations.literal: Hailing feared that grain transport would not keep up and ordered that when the armies crossed the river none might take servants along; those who heard it all murmured in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing supply lines would fail, he forbade servants on the crossing; every soldier who heard it groaned.

sentences.zh: 徒單後與太子光英居守，尚書令張浩、左丞相蕭玉、參知政事敬嗣暉留治省事。

translations.literal: Tushan Hou and the crown prince Guangying remained to guard; Chief Minister Zhang Hao, Left Chancellor Xiao Yu, and Vice Councilor Jing Sihui were left to handle routine business.
translations.idiomatic: Tushan Hou and Crown Prince Guangying stayed behind; Chief Minister Zhang Hao, Left Chancellor Xiao Yu, and Vice Councilor Jing Sihui remained to govern.

sentences.zh: 九月甲午，海陵戎服乘馬，具裝啟行。

translations.literal: On jiawu of the ninth month, Hailing in martial dress mounted horse, fully armored, and set out.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu of the ninth month Hailing mounted in armor and rode out.

sentences.zh: 明日，妃嬪皆行，宮中慟哭久之。

translations.literal: The next day the consorts all departed; within the palace there was long wailing.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the consorts followed; the palace wailed long.

sentences.zh: 十月乙巳，陰晦失路，是夜二更始至蒙城。

translations.literal: On yisi of the tenth month the sky was dark and the way was lost; only at the second watch of that night did they reach Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi of the tenth month, under dark skies they lost the road and did not reach Mengcheng until the second watch.

sentences.zh: 丁未，大軍渡淮，至中流，海陵拜而酹之。

translations.literal: On dingwei the great army crossed the Huai; at midstream Hailing bowed and poured libation.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the main force crossed the Huai; at midstream Hailing bowed and poured a libation.

sentences.zh: 至宿次，見築繚垣者，殺四方館使張永鈐。

translations.literal: At the night's lodging he saw men building stockades and killed the Four Directions Office envoy Zhang Yongqian.
translations.idiomatic: At camp he saw men building stockades and had Zhang Yongqian of the Four Directions Office executed.

sentences.zh: 將至廬州，見白兔，馳射不中。

translations.literal: As they were about to reach Luzhou he saw a white hare and galloped to shoot but did not hit.
translations.idiomatic: Near Luzhou he sighted a white hare, galloped to shoot, and missed.

sentences.zh: 既而後軍獲之以進，海陵大喜，以金帛賜之，顧謂李通曰：「昔武王伐紂，白魚躍於舟中。

translations.literal: Presently the rear guard captured it and presented it; Hailing was greatly pleased, rewarded them with gold and silks, turned and said to Li Tong: "In former days King Wu attacked Zhou — a white fish leapt in the boat."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rear guard caught it and presented it. Hailing rejoiced, gave gold and silk, and told Li Tong, "When King Wu attacked Zhou a white fish leapt into his boat."

sentences.zh: 今朕獲此，亦吉兆也。

translations.literal: Now that I have obtained this, it too is an auspicious omen.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have this—it too is a lucky sign.

sentences.zh: 」癸亥，海陵至和州，百官表奉起居，海陵謂其使：「汝等欲伺我動靜邪？

translations.literal: On guihai Hailing reached Hezhou; the hundred officials submitted a memorial inquiring after his health; Hailing said to their envoy: "Do you wish to spy on my movements?"
translations.idiomatic: On guihai he reached Hezhou; officials sent a health memorial. Hailing told the envoy, "Do you mean to spy on me?"

sentences.zh: 自今勿複來，俟平江南始進賀表。」

translations.literal: From now on do not come again; wait until Jiangnan is pacified before presenting congratulatory memorials."
translations.idiomatic: Do not come again until Jiangnan is pacified—then you may submit congratulations.

sentences.zh: 是時，梁山濼水涸，先造戰船不得進，乃命通更造戰船，督責苛急，將士七八日夜不得休息，壞城中民居以為材木，煮死人膏為油用之。

translations.literal: At this time the waters of Liangshan Marsh had dried up; warships built earlier could not advance; he thereupon ordered Tong to build warships anew, pressing and punishing with harsh urgency; generals and soldiers for seven or eight days and nights had no rest; they destroyed dwellings within the city for timber and boiled dead men's fat for oil.
translations.idiomatic: Liangshan Marsh had run dry and the first warships could not move. Hailing ordered Tong to build new ones with brutal urgency; troops worked seven or eight days without rest, tearing down houses in the city for timber and boiling corpses for ship oil.

sentences.zh: 遂築台于江上，海陵被金甲登臺，殺黑馬以祭天，以一羊一豕投于江中。

translations.literal: Thereupon a platform was built on the river; Hailing in golden armor ascended the platform, killed a black horse to sacrifice to Heaven, and cast one sheep and one pig into the river.
translations.idiomatic: A platform was raised on the river. Hailing in golden armor climbed it, sacrificed a black horse to Heaven, and threw a sheep and a pig into the water.

sentences.zh: 召都督昂、副都督蒲盧渾謂之曰：「舟楫已具，可以濟江矣。

translations.literal: He summoned Commander Ang and Deputy Commander Puluhun and said to them: "The boats are ready — the river may be crossed."
translations.idiomatic: He called Commander Ang and Deputy Commander Puluhun and said, "The fleet is ready—you may cross."

sentences.zh: 」蒲盧渾曰：「臣觀宋舟甚大，我舟小而行遲，恐不可濟。

translations.literal: Puluhun said: "Your servant observes that Song boats are very large; our boats are small and move slowly — I fear they cannot cross."
translations.idiomatic: Puluhun said, "The Song ships are huge; ours are small and slow—I fear we cannot cross."

sentences.zh: 」海陵怒曰：「爾昔從梁王追趙構入海島，豈皆大舟邪？

translations.literal: Hailing said in anger: "In former days you followed Prince Liang in pursuing Zhao Gou to sea-islands — were they all large boats?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing snapped, "When you followed Prince Liang chasing Zhao Gou to the islands, were all their boats large?"

sentences.zh: 明日汝與昂先濟。

translations.literal: Tomorrow you and Ang shall cross first.
translations.idiomatic: Tomorrow you and Ang cross first.

sentences.zh: 」昂聞令己渡江，悲懼欲亡去。

translations.literal: When Ang heard the order that he himself must cross the river, he grieved and feared and wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Ang, hearing he must cross first, was stricken with dread and thought of fleeing.

sentences.zh: 至暮，海陵使謂昂曰：「前言一時之怒耳，不須先渡江也。

translations.literal: At evening Hailing sent to tell Ang: "The words before were a moment's anger — you need not cross the river first."
translations.idiomatic: At evening Hailing sent word to Ang, "That was a flash of temper—you need not cross first."

sentences.zh: 」明日，遣武平軍都總管阿鄰、武捷軍副總管阿撒率舟師先濟。

translations.literal: The next day he dispatched Martial Peace Army Chief Commander A'lin and Martial Swiftness Army Deputy Commander Asa to lead the fleet across first.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent A'lin, chief of the Martial Peace Army, and Asa, deputy of the Martial Swiftness Army, to lead the fleet across first.

sentences.zh: 宿直將軍溫都奧剌、國子司業馬欽、武庫直長習失皆從戰。

translations.literal: Palace Duty General Wendu Aola, Director of the Directorate of Education Ma Qin, and Armory Regular Attendant Xishi all followed in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Duty General Wendu Aola, Directorate of Education director Ma Qin, and Armory Regular Attendant Xishi all went into battle.

sentences.zh: 海陵置黃旗紅旗於岸上，以號令進止，紅旗立則進，黃旗僕則退。

translations.literal: Hailing set yellow flags and red flags on the shore to signal advance and halt; when the red flag stood they advanced, when the yellow flag fell they retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing posted yellow and red flags on the shore to command movement: advance when the red flag went up, fall back when the yellow flag dropped.

sentences.zh: 既渡江，兩舟先逼南岸，水淺不得進，與宋兵相對射者良久，兩舟中矢盡，遂為所獲，亡一猛安、軍士百余人。

translations.literal: Having crossed the river, two boats first pressed the south bank; the water was shallow and they could not advance. They faced Song troops exchanging shots for a long time; the two boats exhausted their arrows and were then captured, losing one meng'an and more than a hundred soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Once across the river, two vessels pushed ahead toward the south bank but grounded in the shallows. They traded fire with Song forces for a long stretch until their arrows were spent; both boats were taken, with the loss of one meng'an and over a hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 海陵遂還和州。

translations.literal: Hailing then returned to Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing withdrew to Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 議定，通複入奏曰：「陛下親師深入異境，無功而還，若眾散於前，敵乘於後，非萬全計。

translations.literal: When the deliberation was settled, Tong again entered to memorialize, saying: 'Your Majesty personally leads the army deep into alien territory and returns without achievement; if the host disperses ahead and the enemy strikes from behind, this is not a plan of complete security.
translations.idiomatic: After the council concluded, Li Tong went in again and said, 'Your Majesty has led the army in person deep into enemy country and now withdraws with nothing gained. If the troops scatter in front while the foe presses from behind, that is no sure plan at all.

sentences.zh: 若留兵渡江，車駕北還，諸將亦將解體。

translations.literal: If troops are left to cross the river while the imperial carriage returns north, the generals too will disband.
translations.idiomatic: Leave men south of the river while the imperial train heads north, and even your commanders will fall apart.

sentences.zh: 今燕北諸軍近遼陽者恐有異志，宜先發兵渡江，斂舟焚之，絕其歸望。

translations.literal: Now the armies north of Yan near Liaoyang may harbor other intentions; you should first send troops across the river, gather the boats and burn them, cutting off their hope of return.
translations.idiomatic: The northern forces near Liaoyang may already be wavering. Send men across the river first, haul the boats in, and burn them—cut off any thought of going home.

sentences.zh: 然後陛下北還，南北皆指日而定矣。

translations.literal: Then Your Majesty returns north; north and south will both be settled within a day.
translations.idiomatic: Only then should Your Majesty ride north. North and south will fall into place in a matter of days.

sentences.zh: 」海陵然之，明日遂趨揚州。

translations.literal: Hailing approved this; the next day he hastened toward Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing agreed. The next day he marched for Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 過烏江縣，觀項羽祠，歎曰：「如此英雄不得天下，誠可惜也。」

translations.literal: Passing Wujiang County, he viewed the shrine of Xiang Yu and sighed, saying: 'So great a hero could not win the realm—truly a pity.'
translations.idiomatic: At Wujiang he stopped at Xiang Yu's shrine and sighed, 'A hero like that—and still he never held the empire. What a waste.'

sentences.zh: 海陵至揚州，使符寶耶律沒答護神果軍扼淮渡，凡自軍中還至淮上，無都督府文字皆殺之。

translations.literal: When Hailing reached Yangzhou, he sent the talisman-and-seal officer Yelü Meda to guard the Shenguo Army at the Huai crossing; anyone returning from the army to the Huai without documents from the supervisory headquarters was to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou he posted Yelü Meda and the Shenguo Army to hold the Huai ford. Any soldier coming back from the front without papers from headquarters was put to death.

sentences.zh: 乃出內箭飾以金龍，題曰禦箭，系帛書其上，使人乘舟射之南岸，其書言「宋國遣人焚毀南京宮室、及沿邊買馬、招誘軍民，今興師問罪，義在吊伐，大軍所至，必無秋毫之犯。

translations.literal: He then took inner arrows adorned with golden dragons, inscribed 'Imperial Arrows,' tied silk letters upon them, and had men in boats shoot them to the south bank. The letter said that Song had sent men to burn the palaces of Nanjing and to buy horses and entice troops and civilians along the border; now he raised the army to demand an accounting, the righteousness lying in succoring the wronged; wherever the great army passed there would assuredly be no violation even of an autumn down.
translations.idiomatic: He had palace arrows fitted with golden dragons, marked Imperial Arrows, and silk messages bound to them shot across to the south bank. The text accused Song of burning the Southern Capital's palaces, buying horses, and luring border troops and civilians—hence this punitive campaign to right wrongs, with a pledge that his army would not harm so much as a hair of the people.

sentences.zh: 」以此招諭宋人。

translations.literal: With this he summoned and instructed the Song people.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he tried to win over the Song side.

sentences.zh: 於是，宋將王權亦縱所獲金軍士三人，齎書數海陵罪，通奏其書，即命焚之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Song general Wang Quan also released three Jin soldiers he had captured, bearing letters enumerating Hailing's crimes; Tong presented the letter and at once ordered it burned.
translations.idiomatic: Song general Wang Quan in turn freed three captured Jin troops carrying a bill of Hailing's crimes. Li Tong brought the document in—and immediately had it burned.

sentences.zh: 海陵怒，亟欲渡江。

translations.literal: Hailing was angry and urgently wished to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing flew into a rage and insisted on forcing a crossing at once.

sentences.zh: 驍騎高僧欲誘其黨以亡，事覺，命眾刃剉之。

translations.literal: The valiant cavalry monk Gaoseng wished to lure his faction to desert; when the affair was discovered, he was ordered dismembered by the multitude with blades.
translations.idiomatic: A bold cavalry monk named Gaoseng tried to coax his comrades into desertion. When the plot surfaced, Hailing had the troops hack him apart with their blades.

sentences.zh: 乃下令，軍士亡者殺其蒲裏衍，蒲裏衍亡者殺其謀克，謀克亡者殺其猛安，猛安亡者殺其總管，由是軍士益危懼。
