translations.literal: He then issued an order: if a soldier fled, his puliyan was killed; if a puliyan fled, his mouke was killed; if a mouke fled, his meng'an was killed; if a meng'an fled, his zongguan was killed. From this the soldiers grew yet more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: He decreed a chain of blood: a deserter's puliyan died, a puliyan's mouke, a mouke's meng'an, a meng'an's zongguan. Terror in the ranks only deepened.

sentences.zh: 甲午，令軍中運鴉鶻船及糧船於瓜州渡，期以明日渡江，敢後者死。

translations.literal: On jiawu day he ordered the army to transport Yaohu boats and grain boats to the Guazhou crossing, fixing the next day for crossing the river; whoever lagged was to die.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiawu he ordered Yaohu craft and grain barges moved to the Guazhou ford, with crossing set for the morrow—delay meant death.

sentences.zh: 乙未，完顏元宜等以兵犯禦營，海陵遇弑。

translations.literal: On yiwei day Wanyan Yuanyi and others with troops attacked the imperial camp; Hailing met assassination.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Wanyan Yuanyi and his men struck the imperial encampment. Hailing was murdered.

sentences.zh: 都督府以南伐之計皆通等贊成之，徒單永年乃其姻戚，郭安國眾所共惡，皆殺之。

translations.literal: The supervisory headquarters held that the plan for the southern campaign had all been advanced by Tong and the rest; Tanshi Yongnian was moreover his affinal kin, and Guo Anguo was universally detested—all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Headquarters blamed the southern war on Li Tong and his circle. Tanshi Yongnian was family by marriage; Guo Anguo was hated by all—each was executed.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，詔削通官爵，人心始快。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, an edict stripped Tong of office and rank; people's hearts at last rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2 an edict stripped Li Tong of rank and title, to the relief of the realm.

sentences.zh: 馬欽，幼名韓哥，嘗仕江南，故能知江南道路。

translations.literal: Ma Qin, childhood name Han Ge, had once served in Jiangnan and therefore knew the roads of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Qin—nicknamed Han Ge in youth—had served in the south and knew its routes.

sentences.zh: 正隆三年，海陵將南伐，遂召用欽，自貴德縣令為右補闕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenglong, as Hailing was about to campaign south, he summoned and employed Qin, promoting him from magistrate of Guide County to Right Subsidiary Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 3, with the southern campaign looming, Hailing called him up from magistrate of Guide to Right Subsidiary Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 欽為人輕脫不識大體，海陵每召見與語，欽出宮輒以語人曰：「上與我論某事，將行之矣。

translations.literal: Qin was by nature frivolous and ignorant of great principle; whenever Hailing summoned him to speak, Qin upon leaving the palace would tell people, saying: 'The Emperor discussed such-and-such a matter with me—it is about to be carried out.'
translations.idiomatic: Qin was flighty and blind to larger stakes. After every audience he would tell others, 'The Emperor and I talked over such-and-such—it's going to happen.'

sentences.zh: 」其視海陵如僚友然。

translations.literal: He regarded Hailing as a colleague among officials.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Hailing like a fellow clerk.

sentences.zh: 累遷國子司業。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to Vice Director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 海陵至和州，欲遣蒲盧渾渡江，蒲盧渾言舟小不可濟，海陵使人召欽，先戒左右曰：「欽若言舟小不可渡江，即殺之。

translations.literal: When Hailing reached Hezhou and wished to send Pulu Hun across the river, Pulu Hun said the boats were small and could not be crossed; Hailing sent for Qin, first warning those beside him: 'If Qin says the boats are small and the river cannot be crossed, kill him at once.'
translations.idiomatic: At Hezhou, when Hailing meant to send Pulu Hun across the river, Pulu Hun said the craft were too small. Hailing sent for Qin, telling his attendants beforehand, 'If he says the boats won't do, kill him.'

sentences.zh: 」欽至，問曰：「此舟可渡江否？

translations.literal: When Qin arrived, he was asked: 'Can these boats cross the river?'
translations.idiomatic: Qin came in and was asked, 'Will these boats carry us across?'

sentences.zh: 」欽曰：「臣得筏亦可渡也。

translations.literal: Qin said: 'Your servant could cross even with a raft.'
translations.idiomatic: Qin answered, 'Give me a raft and I'd still go.'

sentences.zh: 」大定二年，除名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, his name was removed.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2 he was dismissed and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 是日，起前翰林待制大穎為秘書丞。

translations.literal: That same day the former Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders Da Ying was raised to Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: The same day Da Ying, formerly Hanlin Academician Awaiting Orders, was made Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 穎在正隆間嘗言山東盜賊，海陵惡其言，杖之除名。

translations.literal: During Zhenglong Ying had once spoken of bandits in Shandong; Hailing hated his words, beat him with the staff, and removed his name.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenglong years Ying had warned of banditry in Shandong. Hailing took offense, had him beaten, and cashiered him.

sentences.zh: 世宗嘉穎忠直，惡欽巧佞，故複用穎而放欽焉。

translations.literal: Shizong prized Ying's loyalty and uprightness and detested Qin's craft and flattery; therefore he restored Ying and dismissed Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong valued Ying's blunt honesty and loathed Qin's sly flattery—so Ying was brought back and Qin cast out.

sentences.zh: 高懷貞

translations.literal: Gao Huaizhen
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huaizhen

sentences.zh: 高懷貞，為尚書省令史，素與海陵狎昵。

translations.literal: Gao Huaizhen, a clerk of the Department of State Affairs, had long been intimate with Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huaizhen served as a clerk in the Department of State Affairs and had long been on familiar terms with Hailing.

sentences.zh: 海陵久蓄不臣之心，嘗與懷貞各言所志，海陵曰：「吾志有三：國家大事皆自我出，一也。

translations.literal: Hailing for a long time harbored a heart of disloyalty; he once spoke with Huaizhen each of his ambitions, and Hailing said: 'My ambitions are three: that all great affairs of state proceed from me—that is the first.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had long nursed treasonous designs. He and Huaizhen once traded confessions of what each wanted. Hailing said, 'I have three aims: first, that every weighty matter of state issue from my hand alone.

sentences.zh: 帥師伐國，執其君長問罪於前，二也。

translations.literal: To lead armies in attacking states and bring their rulers and chiefs before me to answer for their crimes—that is the second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, to march abroad, conquer, and drag enemy kings before me to answer for their crimes.

sentences.zh: 得天下絕色而妻之，三也。

translations.literal: To obtain the most beautiful women under Heaven and take them to wife—that is the third.'
translations.idiomatic: Third, to take the finest women in the realm for my own.'

sentences.zh: 」由是小人佞夫皆知其志，爭進諛說。

translations.literal: From this the petty men and flatterers all knew his ambition and vied to advance sycophantic counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread among sycophants and small men; they rushed to feed his vanity.

sentences.zh: 大定縣丞張忠輔謂海陵曰：「夢公與帝擊球，公乘馬沖過之，帝墜馬下。

translations.literal: The assistant magistrate of Dading County Zhang Zhongfu said to Hailing: 'I dreamed that the Duke and the Emperor played ball; the Duke rode a horse and charged through; the Emperor fell from his horse.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongfu, assistant magistrate of Dading, told him, 'I dreamed you and the Emperor played cuju. You charged through on horseback and knocked him from his mount.'

sentences.zh: 」海陵聞之大喜。

translations.literal: When Hailing heard this he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was delighted.

sentences.zh: 會熙宗在位久，委政大臣，海陵以近屬為宰相，專威福柄，遂成弑逆之計，皆懷貞輩小人從臾導之。

translations.literal: When Xizong had long held the throne and entrusted government to great ministers, Hailing as a close kinsman became chancellor and monopolized authority and favor, completing the design of regicide—all urged and guided by petty men such as Huaizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong had ruled long and left power to senior ministers. Hailing, a near kinsman, seized the chancellorship and the whip hand of favor, laying the groundwork for murder—urged on at every step by creatures like Huaizhen.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，以懷貞為修起居注，懷貞故父濱州刺史贈中奉大夫。

translations.literal: After Hailing usurped the throne he made Huaizhen Compiler of the Diaries of Activity and Repose; Huaizhen's deceased father, Prefect of Binzhou, was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Master of Palace Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hailing seized the throne he made Huaizhen Compiler of the Imperial Diary and posthumously ennobled his late father, the former prefect of Bin, as Grand Master of Palace Attendance.

sentences.zh: 懷貞累遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Huaizhen was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhen climbed to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，降奉政大夫，放歸田裏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading he was demoted to Grand Master of Governance and sent home to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2 he was reduced to Grand Master of Governance and sent back to his village.

sentences.zh: 五年，與許霖俱賜起複，懷貞為定國軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he and Xu Lin were both granted restoration to office; Huaizhen became Military Commissioner of the Dingguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 5 he and Xu Lin were both recalled; Huaizhen was named military commissioner of the Dingguo Army.

sentences.zh: 上戒之曰：「汝等在正隆時，奸佞貪私，物論鄙之。

translations.literal: The Emperor admonished him, saying: 'You in the Zhenglong years were treacherous, fawning, and greedy; public opinion despised you.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor warned him: 'Under Zhenglong you were treacherous, greedy, and obsequious. Opinion held you in contempt.

sentences.zh: 朕念沒身不齒則無以自新。

translations.literal: I consider that if you are not ranked among the living there is no way to renew yourself.
translations.idiomatic: I thought that unless you were given a second chance you could never reform.

sentences.zh: 若怙舊不悛，必不貸汝矣。」

translations.literal: If you cling to the old ways and do not repent, I will assuredly not spare you.'
translations.idiomatic: Cling to your old ways and I will not spare you.'

sentences.zh: 蕭裕，本名遙折，奚人。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu, original name Yaozhe, was a Xi tribesman.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu, born Yaozhe, was a man of the Xi.

sentences.zh: 初以猛安居中京，海陵為中京留守，與裕相結，每與論天下事。

translations.literal: At first as a meng'an he dwelt at the Central Capital; when Hailing was military commissioner of the Central Capital he bonded with Yu, often discussing affairs under Heaven with him.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a meng'an at the Central Capital. When Hailing was posted there as military commissioner the two became allies and talked endlessly of the empire's future.

sentences.zh: 裕揣海陵有覬覦心，密謂海陵曰：「留守先太師，太祖長子。

translations.literal: Yu divined that Hailing harbored designs of usurpation and secretly said to Hailing: 'The Commissioner is the former Grand Preceptor, the eldest son of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sensed Hailing's ambition and whispered, 'You are the former Grand Preceptor—Taizu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 德望如此，人心天意宜有所屬，誠有志舉大事，顧竭力以從。

translations.literal: With virtue and standing such as this, men's hearts and Heaven's intent ought to turn to you; if you truly have the will to undertake a great affair, I will exhaust my strength to follow.'
translations.idiomatic: Men and Heaven alike should look to you. If you mean to act, I will spend myself in your service.'

sentences.zh: 」海陵喜受之，遂與謀議。

translations.literal: Hailing gladly accepted him and then deliberated with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing welcomed him and they began to plot in earnest.

sentences.zh: 海陵竟成弑逆之謀者，裕啟之也。

translations.literal: That Hailing at last completed the design of regicide—Yu opened it.
translations.idiomatic: It was Yu who first opened the path to regicide.

sentences.zh: 海陵為左丞，除裕兵部侍郎，改同知南京留守事，改北京。

translations.literal: When Hailing was Left Vice Chancellor he appointed Yu Vice Minister of War, then made him Associate Commissioner of the Southern Capital garrison, then transferred him to the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Left Vice Chancellor, Hailing made Yu Vice Minister of War, then associate commissioner at the Southern Capital, then shifted him to the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 海陵領行台尚書省事，道過北京，謂裕曰：「我欲就河南兵建立位號，先定兩河，舉兵而北。

translations.literal: When Hailing headed the Mobile Secretariat of the Department of State Affairs and passed through the Northern Capital, he said to Yu: 'I wish to use the troops south of the river to establish my title, first secure the two He provinces, then raise the army and march north.
translations.idiomatic: Leading the mobile secretariat, he stopped at the Northern Capital and told Yu, 'I mean to raise my standard with the armies south of the river, secure the two He provinces first, then drive north.

sentences.zh: 君為我結諸猛安以應我。

translations.literal: You must rally the meng'an for me in response.'
translations.idiomatic: Rally the meng'an to answer when I call.'

sentences.zh: 」定約而去。

translations.literal: They fixed a covenant and he departed.
translations.idiomatic: They set a date and he moved on.

sentences.zh: 海陵雖自良鄉召還，不能如約，遂弑熙宗篡立，以裕為秘書監。

translations.literal: Although Hailing summoned himself back from Liangxiang, he could not keep the appointment; he then murdered Xizong and usurped the throne, making Yu Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from Liangxiang, he could not keep his promise. He murdered Xizong, seized the throne, and made Yu Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 海陵心忌太宗諸子，欲除之，與裕密謀。

translations.literal: Hailing in his heart feared the sons of Taizong and wished to eliminate them; he conspired secretly with Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He feared Taizong's sons and plotted their ruin with Yu in secret.

sentences.zh: 裕傾險巧詐，因構致太傅宗本、秉德等反狀，海陵殺宗本，唐括辯遣使殺秉德、宗懿及太宗子孫七十余人、秦王宗翰子孫三十餘人。

translations.literal: Yu was devious, treacherous, and crafty; he fabricated evidence of rebellion against the Grand Tutor Zongben, Bingde, and the rest; Hailing killed Zongben, and Tangutuo Bian sent envoys to kill Bingde, Zongyi, and more than seventy sons and grandsons of Taizong, and more than thirty sons and grandsons of Prince Qin Zonghan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was cunning and cruel. He framed the Grand Tutor Zongben, Bingde, and others for treason. Hailing executed Zongben; Tangutuo Bian's agents killed Bingde, Zongyi, more than seventy of Taizong's line, and thirty-odd descendants of Prince Qin Zonghan.

sentences.zh: 宗本已死，裕乃求宗本門客蕭玉，教以具款反狀，令作主名上變。

translations.literal: After Zongben was already dead, Yu then sought out Zongben's retainer Xiao Yu, taught him to draw up a full confession of rebellion, and had him lodge an accusation in his own name.
translations.idiomatic: After Zongben was dead, Yu found his retainer Xiao Yu, coached him to write a full confession of treason, and had him file the denunciation in his own name.

sentences.zh: 海陵既詔天下，天下冤之。

translations.literal: After Hailing had proclaimed this throughout the realm, the realm deemed it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing published the charges across the empire, the outrage was universal.

sentences.zh: 海陵賞誅宗本功，以裕為尚書左丞，加儀同三司，授猛安，賜錢二千萬，馬四百匹、牛四百頭、羊四千口。

translations.literal: Hailing rewarded the merit of executing Zongben, making Yu Left Vice Chancellor, adding the title of Third-Rank Peer, appointing him meng'an, and bestowing twenty million in cash, four hundred horses, four hundred oxen, and four thousand sheep.
translations.idiomatic: For destroying Zongben he made Yu Left Vice Chancellor with the title Third-Rank Peer, named him meng'an, and showered him with twenty million cash, four hundred horses and oxen, and four thousand sheep.

sentences.zh: 再閱月，為平章政事、監修國史。

translations.literal: After another month he became Grand Councilor and Supervisor of the Compilation of National History.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was Grand Councilor and supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 舊制，首相監修國史，海陵以命裕，謂裕曰：「太祖以神武受命，豐功茂烈光于四海，恐史官有遺逸，故以命卿。

translations.literal: By old regulation the chief minister supervised the national history; Hailing gave the charge to Yu and said to Yu: 'Taizu received the mandate through divine martial prowess; his abundant achievements and splendid virtue shine on the four seas—lest the historiographers omit something, I therefore entrust this to you.'
translations.idiomatic: By custom the chief minister oversaw the histories. Hailing handed the task to Yu and said, 'Taizu took the mandate by divine force; his deeds fill the four seas. I fear something may be lost—hence you.'

sentences.zh: 」久之，裕為右丞相、兼中書令。

translations.literal: After a long while Yu became Right Chancellor and concurrently Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In time he rose to Right Chancellor and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 裕在相位，任職用事頗專恣，威福在己，勢傾朝廷。

translations.literal: While Yu held the chancellorship he conducted affairs with considerable arbitrariness; authority and favor rested in himself, and his power overawed the court.
translations.idiomatic: In office Yu acted with little restraint; power and favor pooled in him until he dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 海陵倚信之，他相仰成而已。

translations.literal: Hailing relied on and trusted him; the other chancellors merely nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing leaned on him utterly; other ministers merely assented.

sentences.zh: 裕與高藥師善，嘗以海陵密語告藥師，藥師以其言奏海陵，且曰：「裕有怨望心。

translations.literal: Yu was on good terms with Gao Yaoshi; he once told Yaoshi Hailing's secret words; Yaoshi memorialized these words to Hailing and moreover said: 'Yu harbors resentment.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu was close to Gao Yaoshi and once repeated Hailing's private remarks to him. Yaoshi reported them and added, 'Yu nurses a grudge.'

sentences.zh: 」海陵召裕戒諭之，而不以為罪也。

translations.literal: Hailing summoned Yu to admonish him but did not treat it as a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing summoned Yu, warned him, and let the matter pass.

sentences.zh: 或有言裕擅權者，海陵以為忌裕者眾，不之信。

translations.literal: When some said Yu monopolized power, Hailing thought many envied Yu and did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: When others accused Yu of hoarding power, Hailing judged it mere envy and paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 又以為人見裕弟蕭祚為左副點檢，妹夫耶律辟離剌為左衛將軍，勢位相憑藉，遂生忌嫉，乃出祚為益都尹，辟離剌為甯昌軍節度使，以絕眾疑。

translations.literal: He also thought people saw Yu's younger brother Xiao Zuo as Left Deputy Director of the Palace Inspection and Yu's brother-in-law Yelü Pili as Left Guard General—their positions mutually supporting—and thus jealousy arose; he therefore sent Zuo out as Prefect of Yidu and Pili as Military Commissioner of the Ningchang Army to cut off public suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: He noticed that Yu's brother Xiao Zuo was Left Deputy Director of Palace Inspection and his brother-in-law Yelü Pili Left Guard General—a family bloc—and moved Zuo to prefect of Yidu and Pili to commissioner of Ningchang to quiet suspicion.

sentences.zh: 裕不知海陵意，遽見出其親表補外，不令己知之，自是深念恐海陵疑己。

translations.literal: Yu did not know Hailing's intent and, seeing his close kin and affines posted abroad without letting him know, from this deeply brooded, fearing Hailing suspected him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu did not grasp Hailing's motive. Kin posted abroad without his knowledge fed his fear that the emperor already distrusted him.

sentences.zh: 海陵弟太師袞領三省事，共在相位，以裕多自用，頗防閑之，裕乃謂海陵使袞備之也。

translations.literal: Hailing's younger brother the Grand Preceptor Gun headed the Three Departments and shared the chancellorship; because Yu acted largely on his own, he guarded against him considerably, and Yu then told Hailing that Gun was on guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing's brother Gun, Grand Preceptor, ran the Three Departments and shared power. He checked Yu's independence; Yu told Hailing that Gun was plotting against him.

sentences.zh: 而海陵猜忍嗜殺，裕恐及禍，遂與前真定尹蕭馮家奴、前禦史中丞蕭招折、博州同知遙設、裕女夫遏剌補謀立亡遼豫王延禧之孫。

translations.literal: But Hailing was suspicious, cruel, and addicted to killing; Yu feared disaster and therefore with the former Prefect of Zhending Xiao Feng's slave, the former Censor-in-Chief Xiao Zhaozhe, the Associate Prefect of Bozhou Yaoshe, and Yu's son-in-law Elabu plotted to set up the grandson of the extinct Liao Prince of Yu, the heir Yanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was suspicious and bloodthirsty. Fearful for his life, Yu joined the former prefect Xiao Feng's slave, former censor-in-chief Xiao Zhaozhe, Bozhou associate Yaoshe, and his son-in-law Elabu to place a grandson of the fallen Liao Prince of Yu, heir of Emperor Tianzuo.

sentences.zh: 裕使親信蕭屯納往結西北路招討使蕭好胡，好胡即懷忠。

translations.literal: Yu sent his trusted man Xiao Tunna to win over the Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Xiao Haohu; Haohu was in fact Huaizhong.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Xiao Tunna to the northwestern pacification commissioner Xiao Haohu—known as Huaizhong.

sentences.zh: 懷忠依違未決，謂屯納曰：「此大事，汝歸遣一重人來。

translations.literal: Huaizhong wavered undecided and said to Tunna: 'This is a great affair—you return and send a man of weight.'
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong hesitated. 'This is grave,' he said. 'Send someone with real standing.'

sentences.zh: 」裕乃使招折往。

translations.literal: Yu then sent Zhaozhe.
translations.idiomatic: Yu dispatched Zhaozhe.

sentences.zh: 招折前為中丞，以罪免，以此得詣懷忠。

translations.literal: Zhaozhe had formerly been censor-in-chief and was dismissed for a crime; by this he was able to reach Huaizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaozhe, once censor-in-chief, had been cashiered for crime—his disgrace was his passport to Huaizhong.

sentences.zh: 懷忠問招折與謀者複有何人，招折曰：「五院節度使耶律朗亦是也。

translations.literal: Huaizhong asked Zhaozhe who else was in the plot; Zhaozhe said: 'The Military Commissioner of the Five Circuits Yelü Lang is also among them.'
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong asked who else plotted. Zhaozhe named Yelü Lang, commissioner of the Five Circuits.

sentences.zh: 」懷忠舊與朗有隙，而招折嘗上撻懶變事，懷忠疑招折反復，因執招折，收朗系獄，遣使上變。

translations.literal: Huaizhong had old enmity with Lang, and Zhaozhe had once memorialized on the Tadan rebellion; Huaizhong suspected Zhaozhe of vacillation, therefore seized Zhaozhe, imprisoned Lang, and sent envoys to lodge an accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizhong hated Lang already, and distrusted Zhaozhe for his earlier memorial on the Tadan revolt. He arrested Zhaozhe, jailed Lang, and sent word to the throne.

sentences.zh: 遙設亦與筆硯令史白答書，使白答助裕以取富貴，白答奏其書。

translations.literal: Yaoshe also wrote to the brush-and-ink clerk Bai Da, having Bai Da help Yu to obtain wealth and honor; Bai Da memorialized the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshe wrote the clerk Bai Da, promising riches if he aided Yu. Bai Da turned the letter in.

sentences.zh: 海陵信裕不疑，謂白答構誣之，命殺白答於市。

translations.literal: Hailing trusted Yu and did not doubt him; he thought Bai Da had fabricated slander and ordered Bai Da killed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Still trusting Yu, Hailing took Bai Da's charge for slander and ordered him executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 執白答出宣華門，點檢徒單貞得蕭懷忠上變事入奏，遇見白答，問其故，因止之。

translations.literal: As Bai Da was led out through the Xuanhua Gate, the Director of the Palace Inspection Tanshi Zhen obtained Huaizhong's accusation and entered to memorialize; he met Bai Da and asked the reason, and therefore halted him.
translations.idiomatic: As Bai Da was marched out the Xuanhua Gate, Director Tanshi Zhen arrived with Huaizhong's denunciation, met him on the way, heard his story, and stopped the execution.

sentences.zh: 徒單貞已奏變事，以白答為請，海陵遽使釋之。

translations.literal: Tanshi Zhen had already memorialized the accusation; pleading for Bai Da, Hailing at once sent to release him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had already reported the plot; at his plea Hailing ordered Bai Da freed at once.

sentences.zh: 海陵使宰相問裕，裕即款伏。

translations.literal: Hailing sent the chancellor to question Yu; Yu at once confessed fully.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing sent a chancellor to question Yu, who confessed outright.

sentences.zh: 海陵甚驚愕，猶未能盡信，引見裕，親問之。

translations.literal: Hailing was greatly startled and still could not fully believe; he summoned Yu for a personal audience and questioned him himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was stunned, still half in disbelief. He brought Yu before him and questioned him face to face.

sentences.zh: 裕曰：「大丈夫所為，事至此又豈可諱。

translations.literal: Yu said: 'What a great man does—matters having come to this, how can they be concealed?'
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, 'A man does what he must. At this point, what is there to hide?'

sentences.zh: 」誨陵複問曰：「汝何怨於朕而作此事？

translations.literal: Hailing again asked: 'What grievance do you have against Us that you do this?'
translations.idiomatic: Hailing asked again, 'What grievance drove you to this?'

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「陛下凡事皆與臣議，及除祚等乃不令臣知之。

translations.literal: Yu said: 'Your Majesty discusses everything with your servant, yet when appointing Zuo and the rest you did not let your servant know.
translations.idiomatic: Yu answered, 'Your Majesty consults me on everything—yet you posted Zuo and the others without telling me.

sentences.zh: 領省國王每事謂臣專權，頗有提防，恐是得陛下旨意。

translations.literal: The Director of the Mobile Secretariat, the Prince of the State, on every matter says your servant monopolizes power and guards against me considerably—I fear this is by Your Majesty's instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gun at the mobile secretariat says I hoard power and keeps me at arm's length. I feared that was your will.

sentences.zh: 陛下與唐括辯及臣約同生死，辯以強忍果敢致之死地，臣皆知之，恐不得死所，以此謀反，幸苟免耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with Tangutuo Bian and your servant pledged life and death together; Bian through forceful endurance and daring brought him to death—I know it all—and I feared I would not die a clean death; therefore I rebelled, hoping merely to escape.
translations.idiomatic: You swore life and death with me and Tangutuo Bian. Bian's ruthlessness killed him—and I knew I might be next. I rebelled only to save my skin.

sentences.zh: 太宗子孫無罪，皆死臣手，臣之死亦晚矣。

translations.literal: Taizong's sons and grandsons were innocent—all died by your servant's hand; your servant's death is already late.'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's innocent sons died by my hand. My own death is overdue.'

sentences.zh: 」海陵複謂裕曰：「朕為天子，若于汝有疑，雖汝弟輩在朝，豈不能施行，以此疑我，汝實錯誤。

translations.literal: Hailing again said to Yu: 'We are Son of Heaven; if We had suspicion of you, though your younger brothers and the like were at court, could We not have carried it out? To suspect Us on this account—you were truly mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said again, 'I am emperor. Had I doubted you, could I not have moved against your kin in court? You misread me.

sentences.zh: 太宗諸子豈獨在汝，朕為國家計也。

translations.literal: Taizong's sons and grandsons—were they alone in your hands? We acted for the sake of the state.'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's line was not yours alone to destroy. I acted for the realm.'

sentences.zh: 」又謂之曰：「自來與汝相好，雖有此罪，貸汝性命，惟不得作宰相，令汝終身守汝祖先墳壟。

translations.literal: He again said to him: 'From old We have been on good terms with you; though there is this crime, We spare your life—only you may not be chancellor; We order you to guard your ancestors' graves for life.'
translations.idiomatic: He added, 'We have long been close. For old times' sake I spare your life—but never again as chancellor. Guard your family's graves till you die.'

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「臣子既犯如此罪逆，何面目見天下人，但願絞死，以戒其餘不忠者。

translations.literal: Yu said: 'Your servant having committed such a crime of treachery, with what face can he meet the people under Heaven? He only wishes to be strangled, to warn the rest who are disloyal.'
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, 'After treason such as this, how could I face the world? Strangle me, and let it warn the disloyal.'

sentences.zh: 」海陵遂以刀刺左臂，取血塗裕面，謂之曰：「汝死之後，當知朕本無疑汝心。

translations.literal: Hailing then stabbed his left arm, took blood and smeared it on Yu's face, saying to him: 'After you die you will know that We from the beginning had no heart of suspicion toward you.'
translations.idiomatic: Hailing stabbed his own left arm, smeared the blood on Yu's face, and said, 'When you are dead you will know I never truly doubted you.'

sentences.zh: 」裕曰：「久蒙陛下非常眷遇，仰戀徒切，自知錯繆，雖悔何及。

translations.literal: Yu said: 'Long receiving Your Majesty's extraordinary favor, looking up in passionate longing, knowing himself in error—though he repents, what is there to reach?'
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, 'I enjoyed your extraordinary grace too long. I see my error now—but repentance comes too late.'

sentences.zh: 」海陵哭送裕出門，殺之，並誅遙設及馮家奴。

translations.literal: Hailing wept as he escorted Yu out the door, then killed him, and also executed Yaoshe and Feng's slave.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing wept as he saw Yu out the door, then had him killed, along with Yaoshe and Xiao Feng's slave.

sentences.zh: 馮家奴妻，豫王女也，與其子穀皆與反謀，並殺之。

translations.literal: Feng's slave's wife was a daughter of the Prince of Yu; she and her son Gu were both in the rebellion plot and were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: The slave's wife was a daughter of the Prince of Yu; she and her son Gu had joined the plot and were executed as well.

sentences.zh: 遣護衛龐葛往西北路招討司誅朗及招折，而屯納、遏剌補皆出走，捕得屯納棄市，遏剌補自縊死。

translations.literal: He dispatched the Imperial Guard Pang Ge to the Northwestern Route Pacification Commission to execute Lang and Zhaozhe; Tunna and Elabu both fled; Tunna was captured and exposed in the market, and Elabu hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Imperial Guard Pang Ge to the northwestern pacification commission to kill Lang and Zhaozhe. Tunna and Elabu fled; Tunna was caught and executed in the market, and Elabu hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 屯納出走，過河間少尹蕭之詳，之詳初不知裕事，留之三日。

translations.literal: Tunna fled and passed the Junior Administrator of Hejian Xiao Zhixiang; Zhixiang at first did not know of Yu's affair and kept him three days.
translations.idiomatic: Tunna fled past Hejian's junior administrator Xiao Zhixiang, who at first knew nothing of Yu's plot and sheltered him for three days.

sentences.zh: 屯納往之詳茶紮家，茶紮遣人詣之詳告公引，得之，付屯納遣之他所。

translations.literal: Tunna went to Zhixiang's retainer Chazha's house; Chazha sent a man to Zhixiang to report and lead him out; when he was obtained, he handed Tunna over and sent him elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Tunna went to Zhixiang's retainer Chazha. Chazha sent word to Zhixiang, obtained Tunna, and sent him on elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 茶紮家奴發其事，吏部侍郎窊產鞫之，之祥曰：「屯納宿二日而去。

translations.literal: Chazha's household slave exposed the affair; Vice Minister of Personnel Wachan interrogated; Zhixiang said: 'Tunna lodged two days and departed.'
translations.idiomatic: A slave in Chazha's household exposed the matter. Vice Minister of Personnel Wachan investigated. Zhixiang said, "Tunna stayed two days and left."

sentences.zh: 」法家以之詳隱其間，欺尚書省，罪當贖。

translations.literal: The legalists held that Zhixiang concealed what lay between, deceived the Department of State Affairs, and the crime merited redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Legal officers ruled that Zhixiang had concealed the facts and misled the Department of State Affairs—a crime punishable by fine.

sentences.zh: 海陵怒，命殺之，杖窊產及議法者，茶紮杖四百死。

translations.literal: Hailing was angry and ordered him killed; Wachan and those who deliberated on the law were beaten with the staff; Chazha was beaten four hundred strokes and died.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing ordered Zhixiang executed, had Wachan and the legal officers beaten, and had Chazha beaten four hundred strokes to death.

sentences.zh: 龐葛殺招折等，並殺無罪四人，海陵不問，杖之五十而已。

translations.literal: Pang Ge killed Zhaozhe and the rest, and also killed four innocent men; Hailing did not inquire and only had him beaten fifty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ge killed Zhaozhe and others and four innocent men besides. Hailing ignored the excess and merely had him beaten fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 以裕等罪詔天下。

translations.literal: An edict proclaimed Yu's and the rest's crimes throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict announced Yu's crimes to the empire.

sentences.zh: 賞上變功，懷忠遷樞密副使，以白答為牌印雲。

translations.literal: Those who reported treachery were rewarded; Huaizhong was transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Privy Council; Bai Da was made Keeper of the Seals and Tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Informers were rewarded: Huaizhong became deputy privy council commissioner, and Bai Da was made keeper of the seals.

sentences.zh: 高藥師遷起居注，進階顯武將軍。

translations.literal: Gao Yaoshi was transferred to Compiler of the Diaries of Activity and Repose and advanced in rank to General of Manifest Martiality.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yaoshi was made compiler of the imperial diary and promoted to General of Manifest Martiality.

sentences.zh: 藥師嘗奏裕有怨望，至是賞之雲。

translations.literal: Yaoshi had once memorialized that Yu harbored resentment; now he was rewarded for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yaoshi, who had once reported Yu's discontent, was rewarded at last.

sentences.zh: 胥持國

translations.literal: Xu Chiguo
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chiguo

sentences.zh: 持國為人柔佞有智術。

translations.literal: Chiguo was by nature supple, fawning, and skilled in craft.
translations.idiomatic: Chiguo was pliant, fawning, and clever in intrigue.

sentences.zh: 初，李妃起微賤，得幸於上。

translations.literal: At first Consort Li rose from humble origins and won the Emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Li had begun in low station and won the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 持國久在太子宮，素知上好色，陰以秘術幹之，又多賂遺妃左右用事人。

translations.literal: Chiguo had long been in the Crown Prince's palace and knew well that the sovereign loved beauty; he secretly applied secret arts to win him and also gave many bribes to those about the consort who handled affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Chiguo had long served in the crown prince's household and knew the emperor's appetite for pleasure. He used secret arts to court him and bribed the consort's attendants lavishly.

sentences.zh: 妃亦自嫌門地薄，欲藉外廷為重，乃數稱譽持國能，由是大為上所信任，與妃表裏，筦擅朝政。

translations.literal: The consort also herself felt her family standing was thin and wished to lean on the outer court for weight; she repeatedly praised Chiguo's ability; from this he came to be greatly trusted by the sovereign; with the consort inside and outside in concert, he monopolized court government.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed of her low birth, the consort sought weight through the outer court and praised Chiguo's talents until the emperor trusted him utterly. Consort and favorite worked as one, and he dominated the government.

sentences.zh: 誅鄭王永蹈、鎬王永中，罷黜完顏守貞等事，皆起于李妃、持國。

translations.literal: The executions of Prince of Zheng Yongtao, Prince of Hao Yongzhong, and the dismissal of Wanyan Shouzhen and other affairs all began with Consort Li and Chiguo.
translations.idiomatic: The deaths of Princes Yongtao of Zheng and Yongzhong of Hao, the dismissal of Wanyan Shouzhen, and like crimes all began with Consort Li and Chiguo.

sentences.zh: 士之好利躁進者皆趨走其門下。

translations.literal: Scholar-officials who loved profit and rushed advancement all hurried to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Office-seekers greedy for profit flocked to his door.

sentences.zh: 四方為之語曰：「經童作相，監婢為妃。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm people said of it: 'A classics boy becomes chancellor, a supervising maid becomes consort.'
translations.idiomatic: People said across the realm, "A classics boy for chancellor, a supervising maid for consort."

sentences.zh: 」惡其卑賤庸鄙也。

translations.literal: They detested their base, mean, and vulgar quality.
translations.idiomatic: The saying mocked their base and vulgar rise.

sentences.zh: 承安三年，禦史台劾奏：「右司諫張複亨、右拾遺張嘉貞、同知安豐軍節度使事趙樞、同知定海軍節度使事張光庭、戶部主事高元甫、刑部員外郎張岩叟、尚書省令史傅汝梅、張翰、裴元、郭郛，皆趨走權門，人戲謂'胥門十哲'。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chengan the Censorate impeached, saying: 'Right Department Remonstrator Zhang Fuheng, Right Supplementation Drafter Zhang Jiazhen, Associate Commissioner of the Anfeng Army Military Commission Zhao Shu, Associate Commissioner of the Dinghai Army Military Commission Zhang Guangting, Personnel Section Chief Gao Yuanfu, Penal Code Vice Director Zhang Yansou, Department of State Affairs clerks Fu Rumei, Zhang Han, Pei Yuan, and Guo Ye—all scurry to the gate of power; people jestingly call them the Ten Sages of Xu's Gate.'
translations.idiomatic: In Chengan 3 the censorate impeached Zhang Fuheng, remonstrator of the Right Department; Zhang Jiazhen, supplementation drafter; Zhao Shu and Zhang Guangting, associate military commissioners; Gao Yuanfu, personnel chief; Zhang Yansou, penal vice director; and clerks Fu Rumei, Zhang Han, Pei Yuan, and Guo Ye—all runners at Chiguo's gate, mocked as the "Ten Sages of Xu's Gate."

sentences.zh: 複亨、嘉貞尤卑佞苟進，不稱諫職。

translations.literal: Fuheng and Jiazhen were especially base, fawning, and grasping for advancement, unworthy of remonstrance duties.
translations.idiomatic: Fuheng and Jiazhen were the worst—obsequious climbers unfit for remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 俱宜黜罷。

translations.literal: All should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: All should be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 」奉可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 於是持國以通奉大夫致仕，嘉貞等皆補外。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chiguo retired as Grand Master of Governance for the Imperial Clan, and Jiazhen and the rest were all posted abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Chiguo retired as Grand Master of Governance for the Imperial Clan; Jiazhen and the others were sent to provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 頃之，起知大名府事，未行，改樞密副使，佐樞密使襄治軍於北京。

translations.literal: Before long he was raised to know the affairs of Daming Prefecture; before he departed he was changed to Deputy Commissioner of the Privy Council to assist the Commissioner Xiang in managing troops at Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was named to administer Daming but, before he left, was made deputy privy council commissioner to assist Commissioner Xiang with troops at Beijing.

sentences.zh: 一日，上召翰林修撰路鐸問以他事，因語及董師中、張萬公優劣，鐸曰：「師中附胥持國進。

translations.literal: One day the Emperor summoned Hanlin Compiler Lu Duo to ask about another matter and thereby spoke of the relative merits of Dong Shizhong and Zhang Wangong; Duo said: 'Shizhong advanced by attaching to Xu Chiguo.'
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor summoned Hanlin compiler Lu Duo on another matter and asked him to compare Dong Shizhong and Zhang Wangong. Duo said, "Shizhong rose by clinging to Xu Chiguo."

sentences.zh: 持國奸邪小人，不宜典軍馬，以臣度之，不惟不允人望，亦必不能服軍心，若回日再相，必亂天下。

translations.literal: Chiguo is a treacherous, evil petty man, unfit to command horses and troops; by your servant's estimate, he will not only fail to satisfy men's hopes but surely cannot win the army's hearts; if on his return he becomes chancellor again, he will surely throw the realm into chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Chiguo is a treacherous petty villain, unfit to command armies. He will neither satisfy public expectation nor win the troops. If he becomes chancellor again after this campaign, he will ruin the realm.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「人臣進退人難，人君進退人易，朕豈以此人複為相耶。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'For a minister to advance or dismiss a man is hard; for a ruler to advance or dismiss a man is easy—how could We make this man chancellor again?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Ministers find it hard to move men in or out; for a ruler it is easy. Do you think I would make him chancellor again?"

sentences.zh: 第遷官二階，使之致仕耳。

translations.literal: Only promote him two ranks and let him retire.
translations.idiomatic: I will promote him two ranks and let him retire—that is all.

sentences.zh: 」尋卒於軍，諡曰「通敏」。

translations.literal: Before long he died in the army; his posthumous title was "Penetrating and Keen."
translations.idiomatic: He soon died on campaign; his posthumous title was Penetrating and Keen.

sentences.zh: 後上問平章政事張萬公曰：「持國今已死，其為人竟如何？

translations.literal: Later the Emperor asked Grand Councilor Zhang Wangong: 'Chiguo is now dead—what was his conduct in the end?'
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor asked Grand Councilor Zhang Wangong, "Chiguo is dead—what sort of man was he, after all?"

sentences.zh: 」萬公對曰：「持國素行不純謹，如貨酒平樂樓一事，可知矣。

translations.literal: Wangong answered: 'Chiguo's conduct was never pure and careful; the affair of selling wine at the Pingle Tower shows it.'
translations.idiomatic: Wangong answered, "He was never scrupulous—the Pingle Tower wine-selling affair shows that."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「此亦非好利。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: 'That too is not greed for profit.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is not true greed for profit."

sentences.zh: 如馬琪位參政，私鬻省醖，乃為好利也。

translations.literal: When Ma Qi held the post of Vice Councilor and privately sold the provincial brew—that is greed for profit.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Qi was vice councilor and sold the provincial monopoly brew for himself—that was greed for profit.

sentences.zh: 」子鼎，別有傳。

translations.literal: His son Ding has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding is treated in a separate biography.
